readMe.purpose: Complete readable scientific review and evidence for the revised seven-page paper; proposed formulation awaiting author approval.
readMe.approvalAndScope: This is a private review of an AI-proposed formulation. No author approval, source upload or publication was recorded. Generic “approved” terminology in raw application records is a static library convention and does not establish author approval. Findings remain conditional on the translation faithfully representing the source.
evidencePrecedence: Exact original seven-page PDF and numbered source identify the reviewed manuscript.
The current integrated scientific assessment explains the final scientific standing.
Original outputs, original canonical findings and the original coverage ledger remain preserved as stage-specific records.
Independent manual/SymPy QA is a separately labeled audit; it is not part of the automatic pipeline candidate count.
readMe.stageContext: The author supplied the revised seven-page manuscript, a full-length companion and Appendix I in the handoff. The scalar analysis and original canonical subreport inspected the seven-page manuscript. A statement in that subreport that Appendix I was “not supplied” describes that stage’s evidence, not an absence from the author’s handoff. The final integrated scientific assessment additionally inspected the explicitly listed bounded Appendix I excerpts and a freshly computed restricted symbolic derivation. This is not a review or certification of the entire full-length companion.
readMe.coverageMeaning: The original coverage ledger and its unresolved count classify the pipeline’s translation/checking scope; they are not a count of false claims or manuscript defects. The later integrated assessment and source judgments take precedence for the current scientific interpretation. The separate AST audit identifies bookkeeping cases without changing the saved original package or checker report.
readMe.editorialQAContext: The independent Hayward wording assessment is separately attributed in independentQA.integratedAssessmentEditorial. It does not override the exact saved model judgment or readiness.
readMe.thirdPartyEvidence: Original scientific findings and judgments are retained. Long external primary-source passage bodies are omitted from this shareable export, with URLs, SHA identities, exact locators and the redaction manifest preserved. Author-supplied manuscript and Appendix I context are included.
excludedCategories: Provider credentials, cookies, private session data, environment configuration and transport headers
Raw unaccepted model hypotheses and duplicated request/response captures
Unrelated papers and earlier one-page review evidence

Boundary Potential
J. T. Tyler
La Jolla, California, USA; revised 28 October 2026
Abstract
Recognizing acceleration length as a geometrically normalized work coordinate of the established Einstein
boundary potential identifies a new generalized boundary force and normal-scale pressure. These join
the area-conjugate surface stress in one macroscopic state law. The selected nonexpanding-null action
response supplies the principal canonical justification; the stationary area–boost route gives a complementary
interpretation with shared clock and area normalization. Schwarzschild work becomes M κ dR = P R dV , with
P R = 2 P L . The separately assigned instantaneous equilibrium FRW screen has P R = P L = ρ/ 3 and potential
equal to the Misner–Sharp horizon energy. Temperature and entropy enter after the mechanics. The result
concerns a specified boundary prescription, not a new interaction or an unrestricted moving-horizon theorem.

Horizon Boundary Mechanics: Force, Pressure, and Work from the Einstein
Boundary Potential
J. T. Tyler
La Jolla, California, USA; revised 28 October 2026
Abstract
Recognizing acceleration length as a geometrically normalized work coordinate of the established Einstein
boundary potential identifies a new generalized boundary force and normal-scale pressure. These join
the area-conjugate surface stress in one macroscopic state law. The selected nonexpanding-null action
response supplies the principal canonical justification; the stationary area–boost route gives a complementary
interpretation with shared clock and area normalization. Schwarzschild work becomes M κ dR = P R dV , with
P R = 2 P L . The separately assigned instantaneous equilibrium FRW screen has P R = P L = ρ/ 3 and potential
equal to the Misner–Sharp horizon energy. Temperature and entropy enter after the mechanics. The result
concerns a specified boundary prescription, not a new interaction or an unrestricted moving-horizon theorem.

selectedInputs.title: Constants and scalar domains
selectedInputs.statement: Hold c and G fixed. Positive c, G and finite positive cut area are inferred physical domains; the length-coordinate chart excludes κ = 0.

selectedInputs.title: Signed acceleration length and clock
selectedInputs.statement: Use the specified physical time normalization of κ, signed L_s = c²/κ, and magnitude L_κ = |L_s|. Do not identify L_κ with a universal spherical radius.

selectedInputs.title: Einstein boundary potential
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt U_∂(A,L_s) = c⁴A/(8πG L_s), equivalently the stated area–surface-gravity expression, for the selected Einstein boundary prescription.

selectedInputs.title: Independent mechanical coordinates
selectedInputs.statement: Differentiate in independent (A,L_s) before imposing a horizon-family relation. Define Π_∂ by the A derivative and F_L by the negative L_s derivative; P_L is force per cut area.

selectedInputs.title: Mass equivalent and Einstein coupling
selectedInputs.statement: Use M_∂ = U_∂/c² and κ_E = 8πG/c⁴.

selectedInputs.title: Null geometry
selectedInputs.statement: N is null, foliated by spacelike two-cuts S with metric q_AB and area element ε_S. ξ is a selected null generator; its inaffinity is κ̂ and expansion is θ, with physical κ = c²κ̂.

selectedInputs.title: Null scalar canonical prescription
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt μ = κ̂ + θ/2 and the cited scalar area polarization. In c = 1 units, add δB_μ to exchange the area and rate polarizations; other canonical sectors remain present.

selectedInputs.title: Restricted nonexpanding variations
selectedInputs.statement: Restrict to θ = 0 and tangent variations δθ = 0, preserving nullness. Fix the clock prescription, cuts and interval; control other responses while retaining matter and other sectors.

selectedInputs.title: Physical-clock null response
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt the oriented scalar response Θ_κ^(0) = (c²/(8πG))∫dτ∫_S ε_S δκ under the prescribed conversion to acceleration units and physical time.

selectedInputs.title: Selected action and endpoints
selectedInputs.statement: The companion calculation uses fixed Gaussian-null gauge and I_rate = I_EH − B_0 + B_μ. In c = 1 units its endpoint shift is −(A_f−A_i)/(16πG); orientation, clock, domain and other responses are retained.

selectedInputs.title: Uniform-cut reduction
selectedInputs.statement: For a common length variation integrate the pressure density over S. For uniform finite cuts use F_L = AP_L; uniform stationary data permit division by the fixed duration Δτ.

selectedInputs.title: Stationary area–boost normalization
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt a spacelike-corner area–boost pair with orientation consistent with equation (15), J_η = Ac³/(8πG), and stationary rate ω_s = κ/c for the same normalized clock.

selectedInputs.title: Fixed stationary duration
selectedInputs.statement: For the area–boost interpretation hold Δτ fixed and use η = cΔτ/L_s.

selectedInputs.title: Rindler normalization
selectedInputs.statement: Use a uniformly accelerated observer with constant positive proper acceleration a in Minkowski spacetime, its orthogonal instantaneous rest slice, κ = a and independent planar area.

selectedInputs.title: Spherical marginal-horizon geometry
selectedInputs.statement: On a spherical marginal horizon use A = 4πR² and E_MS = c⁴R/(2G). The restriction is not an arbitrary-sphere energy formula.

selectedInputs.title: Schwarzschild family
selectedInputs.statement: Use stationary Killing time normalized at infinity, A_H = 4πR_H², κ = c²/(2R_H), L_κ = 2R_H and U_∂ = Mc²/2.

selectedInputs.title: Schwarzschild mass-radius compatibility
selectedInputs.statement: For a scalar translation using both M and R_H, infer the usual compatibility Mc² = c⁴R_H/(2G). This is not printed as a standalone equation.

selectedInputs.title: Areal-volume work convention
selectedInputs.statement: For a sphere use areal volume 4πR³/3 and dV = A dR. In independent (A,L_s) space, A dL_s is only the stipulated work one-form ϑ_V.

selectedInputs.title: FRW geometric setting
selectedInputs.statement: Use four-dimensional FRW with arbitrary spatial curvature, H = ȧ/a and R_A = c/√(H²+kc²/a²). A real positive horizon requires a positive radicand.

selectedInputs.title: Einstein–FRW matter identification
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G), E_A = ρV_A and V_A = 4πR_A³/3. Here ρ and p_m are bulk energy density and pressure in the same units; V_A is areal, not generally proper spatial, volume.

selectedInputs.title: Instantaneous Cai–Kim screen
selectedInputs.statement: Separately assign κ_CK = c²/R_A and L_CK = R_A for the instantaneous equilibrium FRW screen. This is not a deduction that its evolving worldtube is nonexpanding and null.

selectedInputs.title: FRW dynamical input
selectedInputs.statement: The curvature, acceleration and screen-pressure evolution relations (35)–(37) are asserted as a representation of Einstein–Friedmann dynamics, not consequences of pressure definition alone.

selectedInputs.title: Signed Hayward calibration
selectedInputs.statement: Use the signed Hayward rate ratio in equation (38), w = p_m/ρ and the nonzero-rate branch for equation (39). Do not replace its signed radial response by the nonnegative quadratic normal response.

selectedInputs.title: Thermal state normalization
selectedInputs.statement: A regular Hawking–Unruh/KMS state separately supplies Ω_κ = |κ|/c, Euclidean period cΔτ_E = 2πL_κ and k_B T = ℏΩ_κ/(2π).

selectedInputs.title: Einstein entropy convention
selectedInputs.statement: Adopt Einstein entropy with zero additive constant, expressed by S/k_B = 2πJ_η/ℏ, and ℓ_P² = Gℏ/c³.

selectedInputs.title: Positive thermal branch
selectedInputs.statement: Use κ > 0, hence L_s = L_κ, for equations (22), (41) and the positive-temperature mechanical identification.

selectedInputs.title: Scalar translation of differential coefficients
selectedInputs.statement: For bounded scalar checks, interpret ordinary mechanical differentials through their derivative coefficients before family substitution. Retain functional, tensor, integral and exterior-form claims outside that scalar proof.

selectedInputs.title: Radiation specialization for the Hayward comparison
selectedInputs.statement: To translate the source's named radiation-FRW example into equation (38), infer w = 1/3. This premise is not printed separately in the supplied manuscript.

selectedInputs.title: De Sitter specialization for the Hayward comparison
selectedInputs.statement: To translate the source's named de Sitter example into equation (38), infer w = −1. This premise is not printed separately in the supplied manuscript.

proposedFormulation.mainClaim: For a specified Einstein boundary potential and selected nonexpanding-null action prescription, acceleration length is proposed as a geometrically normalized work coordinate, with a length-conjugate force and normal-scale pressure. The paper develops conditional mechanical identities, Schwarzschild radius-work identities, and separately assigned instantaneous Cai–Kim FRW screen identities.
assumptions: Model 1: This proposed translation adopts the specified Einstein boundary prescription; it does not derive that prescription from an action or establish its canonical justification.
Model 1: c and G are fixed positive physical constants. A is a finite positive cut area. Their positive domains are disclosed physical-domain choices, not recorded author approvals.
Model 1: A and L_s are independent differentiation coordinates, with L_s nonzero and of either sign. No horizon-family relation between them is imposed.
Model 1: The source coordinate relation L_s=c²/κ is represented equivalently by the adopted definition κ=c²/L_s on the nonzero chart. The specified physical time normalization is retained.
Model 1: U_b is defined using the source's area–surface-gravity formula, not its length-coordinate formula. The latter is a proposed substitution check.
Model 1: All declared derived dependencies are expanded during differentiation. In particular, κ varies with L_s and is not held independent when differentiating U_b with respect to L_s.
Model 1: Pi_b is the A derivative of U_b at fixed L_s; F_L is the negative L_s derivative at fixed A; P_L is F_L/A. These response conventions are adopted premises.
Model 1: M_b=U_b/c² and kappa_E=8πG/c⁴ are adopted conventions. They do not introduce a material equation of motion.
Model 1: pi denotes the usual fixed positive dimensionless mathematical constant. Response symbols have real domains so that their signs are not assumed as conclusions.

Model 2: Use fixed positive c and G and the positive dimensionless circle constant pi. Positive finite cut area A is a proposed physical domain choice, not an independently established source conclusion.

Model 2: Keep A and signed Ls independent. Restrict Ls to nonzero values and use the inverse acceleration-length chart kappa=c^2/Ls with the source's specified physical clock. No horizon-family relation between A and Ls is imposed.

Model 2: Adopt the Einstein boundary potential in equation (2). Adopt the explicit stress and pressure formulas in equations (4) and (6); define FL independently by the negative Ls derivative of the potential. Adoption of these formulas is not an independent verification of their gravitational justification.

Model 2: For the canonical interpretation, adopt the source's null hypersurface and spacelike cuts, selected generator, nonexpanding sector theta=0, and tangent variations delta theta=0. Preserve nullness and retain matter and other responses while controlling the other boundary data.

Model 2: Adopt the selected rate-action prescription I_rate=I_EH-B_0+B_mu, its orientation, fixed clock, cuts and interval, and its stated endpoint prescription. These physical choices are not derived from the potential.

Model 2: Adopt equation (14) as the physical canonical input: the response density multiplying delta kappa and the area and physical-time measures is c^2/(8*pi*G). The scalar checks do not establish this boundary one-form.
Model 2: Use a common length variation and, where the integrated scalar response is discussed, a uniform finite cut. The stationary duration dt is positive and fixed.
Model 2: For the complementary stationary route, adopt the matched corner orientation, Jeta=A*c^3/(8*pi*G), and omega=kappa/c for the same area normalization and physical clock.
Model 2: Adopt the stationary boost relation eta=c*dt/Ls. Its differentiation holds dt and all other independent scalars fixed.
Model 2: The independent kappa_src is an alternate source-chart coordinate, not an additional physical degree of freedom. Coordinate substitutions explicitly relate it to kappa or Ls.

Model 2: At fixed A and controlled other data, integrate the adopted equation-(14) response over the fixed stationary interval. I_src is only a primitive of this source-restricted first variation: I0+dt*A*Rk*kappa_src, with I0 independent of the acceleration-length source. This does not assume the desired length-force derivative or specify the complete on-shell action.

Model 2: Ios denotes that restricted primitive after the explicit substitution kappa_src=kappa. No physical interpretation of its A derivative is asserted; a length-independent remainder can depend on other fixed data.

Model 2: Ordinary derivatives translate scalar differential coefficients. Integral, functional-derivative, tensor and exterior-form statements retain their separate physical and mathematical requirements.
Model 3: This is a proposed private scalar translation for group g03, not an author-approved formulation or a verification of the manuscript.
Model 3: For c025 and c263, A and Lk are independent positive scalar coordinates. Work only on the source's positive branch, where L_s = L_κ = Lk and κ > 0. No horizon-family relation is imposed.
Model 3: Hold c, G, hbar, kB and pi fixed during differentiation. Use their usual positive physical values; pi is the positive symbolic circle constant. Positive area excludes degenerate cuts.
Model 3: For c012, use κ = c²/L_s as the inverse-coordinate definition of L_s = c²/κ. L_s is an alias of the independent coordinate Lk, not an additional independent variable.
Model 3: For c020, adopt the selected Einstein boundary potential U = c⁴A/(8πG L_s), equivalently Aκc²/(8πG). Its physical prescription and normalization are inputs.

Model 3: For c029, c032 and c036, define the area response by Pi = ∂U/∂A, the length response by F = −∂U/∂Lk, and pressure by P = F/A. On this branch, differentiation in Lk is the stated differentiation in L_s.

Model 3: For c110 and c111, adopt J = Ac³/(8πG) and omega = κ/c for the same normalized stationary clock and the source's canonical orientation. The canonical meaning of J is not established by scalar algebra.

Model 3: For c258, c259 and c261, adopt the separate regular Hawking–Unruh/KMS thermal dictionary: Omega = κ/c on the positive branch and T = hbar·Omega/(2πkB). This does not establish applicability to an arbitrary evolving horizon.
Model 3: For c262, adopt Einstein entropy S = 2πkB J/hbar with zero additive constant. No entropy normalization is inferred from the mechanical potential alone.
Model 3: For c260, adopt the Euclidean regularity relation through tauE = 2πLk/c. This is a physical input, not a derived regularity theorem.
Model 3: For c269, adopt ellP2 = G·hbar/c³. Scalar differential identities below mean equality of coefficients in the independent coordinates A and Lk.
Model 4: All proposed equalities are conditional on this translation faithfully representing the specified Schwarzschild model; none establishes the physical premises independently.
Model 4: The constants c, G, hbar and kB have their conventional physical meanings and are fixed and positive. pi is the fixed positive mathematical constant, kept symbolic.

Model 4: A, L_s and R_H are independent scalar coordinates during differentiation: A>0, L_s is nonzero and signed, and R_H>0. No area–length family constraint is imposed before the partial derivatives of U.
Model 4: Adopt the Einstein boundary potential U=c^4 A/(8 pi G L_s), the conventions Pi_b=partial U/partial A and F_L=-partial U/partial L_s, and the density P_L=F_L/A.
Model 4: For the Schwarzschild family, adopt infinity-normalized stationary Killing time and kappa=c^2/(2 R_H). This gravitational relation is an input, not derived from the potential.
Model 4: Adopt A_H=4 pi R_H^2 and the areal volume V_H=4 pi R_H^3/3. Areal volume and areal radius are not asserted to be proper spatial volume or universal proper distance.

Model 4: The family has positive kappa. Thus its signed acceleration length and magnitude coincide, and the family substitution is L_s=L_k with L_k=c^2/kappa. L_k=2 R_H is not adopted as a definition.

Model 4: Adopt the inferred Schwarzschild compatibility M=c^2 R_H/(2 G). This is an additional disclosed family premise supported by the source's mass and marginal-horizon formulas, not a separately printed mass–radius equation or an independently established result.
Model 4: Adopt E=M c^2. Define U_H by substituting the family area and acceleration length into U; do not assume U_H=M c^2/2.

Model 4: Use the separately stated radial formula F_R=M kappa as an adopted comparison formula, and P_R=F_R/A_H as its density convention. The work-coefficient claims test compatibility with these formulas rather than assuming F_R=2 F_L.

Model 4: Adopt the additional positive-branch Hawking–Unruh temperature T=hbar kappa/(2 pi c kB), the corner normalization J_eta=A_H c^3/(8 pi G), and Einstein entropy S=2 pi kB J_eta/hbar with zero additive constant.

Model 4: Every derivative along R_H holds the physical constants fixed. Ordinary differential statements are translated into scalar coefficient equalities; this does not translate their Hamiltonian, canonical or covariant foundations.
Model 5: Hold c and G fixed and positive. Treat pi as the fixed positive, dimensionless circle constant, without a rational approximation.

Model 5: Differentiate the generic potential in independent A > 0 and nonzero signed L_s before imposing any family relation. The source relation κ = c²/L_s is expanded directly into the potential definition.
Model 5: Adopt the specified Einstein boundary potential U_base = c⁴A/(8πG L_s) as a physical input, not as a result established by these scalar comparisons.

Model 5: Use an independent positive family coordinate R_A. Adopt spherical marginal-horizon area A_A = 4πR_A² and areal volume V_A = 4πR_A³/3; this volume is not asserted to be proper spatial volume.
Model 5: Separately adopt the instantaneous Cai–Kim assignments κ_CK = c²/R_A and L_CK = R_A. They are not inferred from the nonexpanding-null action prescription.
Model 5: Adopt the geometric energy E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G) and the Einstein matter–geometry identification E_A = ρV_A. Encode the latter by defining ρ = E_A/V_A, rather than leaving ρ independent.
Model 5: Adopt M_A = E_A/c² and the notation P_scr = P_L_CK.
Model 5: Define the area response and length force by the independent-coordinate derivatives of U_base, followed by explicit family substitution. Define normal pressure as force divided by cut area.

Model 5: Translate radius work through F_R = F_L dL_CK/dR_A and P_R = F_R/A_A, using the spherical areal-volume convention dV_A = A_A dR_A. These are scalar work-coordinate conventions, not a covariant action derivation.

Model 5: Positive domains for geometric quantities, energy, density and mass follow the adopted positive-radius branch and definitions. Response symbols are declared real without imposing their proposed coefficient formulas as domain constraints.

definitions.description: Adopt the inverse-coordinate representation κ=c²/L_s of c012, with the nonzero chart c014. It is equivalent to L_s=c²/κ because c is positive and L_s is nonzero. The sign of κ follows the sign of L_s. Source: p1-l024, p1-l026–p1-l029.
Adopt c022, κ_E=8πG/c⁴, as the source's coupling convention. Its positive domain follows from the declared positive constants. Source: p1-l018–p1-l019.

Adopt the physical input c020, U_∂=Aκc²/(8πG), for the specified boundary prescription. This does not adopt c021 as a defining equality; c021 is proposed below as the coordinate-substitution check. Source: p1-l039, p1-l041, p1-l043–p1-l047.
Adopt c028, M_∂=U_∂/c², as a potential-mass convention, not an independently specified material mass. Source: p2-l001–p2-l003.

Adopt c029: Π_∂ is the partial derivative of U_∂ with respect to independent A, holding L_s and the physical constants fixed. This is a response definition, not an independent canonical derivation. Source: p2-l005, p2-l007–p2-l011.

Adopt c032: F_L is minus the partial derivative of U_∂ with respect to independent L_s, holding A and the physical constants fixed. The minus sign is the source's work convention. Source: p2-l015–p2-l018.
Adopt c036, P_L=F_L/A, as a force-per-cut-area response convention. No material-pressure interpretation or independent canonical pair is assumed. Source: p2-l025–p2-l028.
Adopt the inverse of equation (1), kappa=c^2/Ls, on its nonzero signed chart (c012, c014). This is a coordinate definition with the prescribed clock, not a horizon-family constraint.
Adopt equation (2), U=c^4*A/(8*pi*G*Ls), as the specified boundary potential. Its sign follows the signed length chart; its physical normalization is an input.
Adopt the oriented physical-clock coefficient c^2/(8*pi*G) from equation (14), p2-l064 through p2-l072 (c081). Area and time measures are not included in Rk.

Adopt the explicit equation-(4) value Pi=kappa*c^2/(8*pi*G) (c031). This batch differentiates that source-stated formula; it does not separately propose a claim establishing its area-derivative origin.

Adopt the explicit equation-(6) pressure formula (c038). Its positivity follows from the declared domains and Ls^2. Its equality to derivative force per area is proposed separately in g02_uniform_force.

Use the source's convention FL=-partial U/partial Ls at fixed independent A, c and G. The declared positive domain follows from differentiating the adopted potential on A>0 and Ls!=0, rather than from a material equation of motion.
Adopt the action-valued corner normalization Jeta=A*c^3/(8*pi*G) from equation (18) (c110), with the source's matched orientation and area normalization. The canonical corner pair is a cited input.
Adopt omega=kappa/c from equation (18) (c111), for the same stationary physical clock. Its length-coordinate expression is a separate candidate.
Adopt equation (20), eta=c*dt/Ls, with dt fixed (c118). This is a stationary boost prescription, not an assertion that every prescribed cut rate is an evolution rate.

Choose a primitive of the adopted uniform stationary equation-(14) source response at fixed A and controlled other data: I0+dt*A*Rk*kappa_src. Integration is possible because dt*A*Rk is independent of kappa_src. I0 is an arbitrary source-independent offset. Explicitly pull the restricted source primitive back by kappa_src=kappa=c^2/Ls. The c313 candidate differentiates this expression and compares it with the independently defined potential force; its desired derivative is not adopted as a definition.
Adopt L_s = L_κ on the positive branch (c012, c263; equation (1) and the qualification preceding equation (41)). Ls is only an alias; differentiation uses independent Lk.
Encode c012 by the inverse relation κ = c²/L_s. This adopts the source's specified physical-time normalization; κ is not an independent differentiation variable.
Adopt c269, ℓ_P² = G hbar/c³, from equation (42).
Adopt the source potential in equation (2), c020. With the adopted κ definition, this is also Aκc²/(8πG). The Einstein boundary prescription is a premise, not a scalar conclusion.
Adopt c029: the A derivative at fixed Lk, equivalently fixed L_s. Differentiating the adopted potential gives c⁴/(8πG Lk), positive on the stated chart.

Adopt c036, P_L = F_L/A. This is a response-density definition, not an additional canonical pair or a material equation of motion.
Adopt c110, J_η = Ac³/(8πG), from equation (18), with the source's corner orientation and shared area normalization. The physical area–boost foundation remains an input.

Adopt c262, S/kB = 2πJ_η/hbar, with the explicit zero additive constant. This independently supplied entropy dictionary gives S = kB Ac³/(4G hbar).
Encode the adopted Euclidean regularity premise c260, c Δτ_E = 2πL_κ. No candidate purports to derive Euclidean regularity.
Adopt the source's areal-radius convention A_H=4 pi R_H^2, equation (25). This defines the family area without constraining independent A before differentiation.
Adopt V_H=4 pi R_H^3/3 as the source's spherical areal-volume convention after equation (27). Its derivative is not separately assumed.
Adopt kappa=c^2/(2 R_H), equation (25), with the stated infinity-normalized Killing clock. Here kappa denotes only this family quantity.
Adopt the acceleration-length definition c^2/kappa on the positive Schwarzschild branch. It equals both L_s on this family and its magnitude; the output L_k=2 R_H is not assumed.

Adopt the explicitly disclosed inference M=c^2 R_H/(2 G). The source gives the marginal-horizon energy and Schwarzschild mass formulas but not this standalone equation. This premise is not inferred here by assuming the candidate U_H=M c^2/2.
Adopt the source's mass-energy convention E=M c^2 in section 4.
Adopt the length-coordinate form of the selected Einstein boundary potential, equation (2). A and L_s remain independent; U can have either sign because L_s is signed.
Adopt Pi_b=partial U/partial A at fixed L_s, c and G, equation (4). This is a derivative convention, not an independent canonical justification.
Adopt F_L=-partial U/partial L_s at fixed A, c and G, equation (5). Family substitution is applied to this derivative afterward, not to U before the partial derivative.
Adopt the pressure-density convention P_L=F_L/A, equation (6). It is not a separate canonical pair.
Restrict the independent-coordinate potential to A=A_H and L_s=L_k only after defining its independent-coordinate responses. No mass-energy value for U_H is assumed.

Adopt the separately stated formula F_R=M kappa from equation (27) as a comparison input. Claims test its agreement with the differentiated length response; F_R=2 F_L and F_R=F_L dL_k/dR_H are not used as definitions.
Adopt P_R=F_R/A_H, the source's density convention in equation (27). The transformed relation P_R=2 P_L is not assumed.
Adopt the independent thermal dictionary kB T=hbar kappa/(2 pi c) on the positive branch, equation (40). It is not derived from the mechanical potential.
Adopt the area–boost normalization J_eta=A_H c^3/(8 pi G), equation (18), restricted to this family. Its canonical origin is not established by scalar algebra.

Adopt S/kB=2 pi J_eta/hbar, equation (40), with the source's zero additive entropy constant. Together with the adopted J_eta normalization this is Einstein area entropy, not a result inferred from TS=U_H.
Adopt Eq. (2), with κ = c²/L_s expanded into Aκc²/(8πG). A and L_s remain independent here; the potential can be signed when L_s is signed.
Adopt the spherical marginal-horizon areal-radius convention A_A = 4πR_A².
Adopt Eq. (30)'s areal volume V_A = 4πR_A³/3, not a general proper-spatial-volume formula.
Adopt the separate instantaneous CK calibration L_CK = R_A from Eq. (31).
Adopt Eq. (31)'s positive CK rate κ_CK = c²/R_A with its specified normalization.
Adopt the source convention κ_E = 8πG/c⁴.
Adopt Eq. (30)'s geometric marginal-horizon energy E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G). This is not derived from screen pressure.
Encode the adopted Einstein matter–geometry input E_A = ρV_A by solving it for ρ on the positive-volume branch. Density is therefore not an additional independent coordinate in this family.
Adopt the stated convention M_A = E_A/c².
Restrict the adopted generic potential by A = A_A and L_s = L_CK. Equality to E_A is not imposed in this definition.
Adopt Π_∂ = ∂U_base/∂A at fixed L_s. Differentiate first, then evaluate on the CK family; do not differentiate an area-radius-constrained potential to define this response.
Adopt F_L = −∂U_base/∂L_s at fixed A, followed by the explicit CK substitutions. The constant-force formula in Eq. (32) is not assumed.
Define the scalar radius-work coefficient by F_L dL_CK = F_R dR_A along this family. Equality F_R = F_L is left for the Jacobian comparison.
Adopt the normal-response density convention P_L = F_L/A, evaluated on the positive-area CK family.
Adopt Eq. (32)'s notation P_scr = P_L_CK. This alias alone is not an independent verification.
Define the pressure coefficient for radius work using F_R dR_A = P_R dV_A and the spherical convention dV_A = A_A dR_A. No equality to P_L_CK or P_scr is imposed here.

claims.title: Boundary potential in the signed length coordinate
claims.explanation: Proposed check of c021: substitute the adopted κ=c²/L_s into the independently stated area–κ form of the potential. This tests the coordinate rewrite, not the physical justification of the potential.

claims.title: Independent-area coefficient of the mechanical differential
claims.explanation: Differentiate the adopted potential with respect to independent A at fixed L_s,c,G. This supplies the dA coefficient of c026. By the adopted definition of Pi_b, it also supplies the dA coefficient of c027; the derivative convention itself is not independently verified.

claims.title: Independent-length coefficient of the mechanical differential
claims.explanation: Differentiate with respect to independent L_s at fixed A,c,G, including κ's declared dependence on L_s. This supplies the signed dL_s coefficient of c026 and, through the adopted negative-derivative definition of F_L, the dL_s coefficient of c027.

claims.title: Area response equals potential per area
claims.explanation: Evaluate the adopted area derivative and compare it with U_b/A, establishing the proposed c030 identity conditionally on the potential. Because A is positive, c042, U_b=Pi_b A, is the equivalent multiplicative form, not a separate independent check.

claims.title: Area response in the surface-gravity normalization
claims.explanation: Evaluate the area derivative and compare it with the independently printed κ-normalized coefficient c031. Under the adopted definitions of κ and κ_E, multiplying this equality by κ_E gives c048, 1/L_s=κ_E Pi_b; that is an equivalent scale form, not an additional candidate.

claims.title: Length response equals potential per signed length
claims.explanation: Evaluate minus the independent-length derivative and compare it with U_b/L_s for c033. Multiplication by nonzero L_s gives c043. Substituting the adopted P_L=F_L/A then gives c044, U_b=P_L A L_s. These product forms are algebraic restatements, not additional independent checks.

claims.title: Boundary response and potential-mass identity
claims.explanation: Compare the evaluated negative length derivative with the product of the separately adopted potential-mass convention and coordinate-normalized κ. This is c034 as a scalar identity; it is not a material acceleration law.

claims.title: Normal response density from area stress and signed length
claims.explanation: Evaluate the two derivative-defined responses and the adopted force-per-area density, then compare P_L with Pi_b/L_s. This is the scalar identity c037, conditional on the common potential.

claims.title: Explicit normal response density in length coordinates
claims.explanation: Compute minus the length derivative of the potential and divide by positive A. The proposed equality is c038; its explicit inverse-square expression is not assumed in the definition of P_L.

claims.title: Quadratic surface-gravity response density
claims.explanation: Compare the derivative-defined density with the source's κ²/(8πG) formula using the disclosed coordinate relation. This proposes c039 for either sign of L_s; no positive-κ branch is imposed.

claims.title: Length coefficient of the stress differential
claims.explanation: Differentiate the area response with respect to L_s at fixed A. This proposes the L_s coefficient of c046. Multiplication by A and the adopted P_L=F_L/A gives the L_s coefficient of c045. The separate zero dA coefficient of these unrestricted two-coordinate differentials is not an additional candidate here and is recorded as residual coverage.

claims.title: Inverse-square scale law from the common mechanics
claims.explanation: Substitute the adopted Einstein coupling and the derivative-defined response density, then cancel the fixed factors. This is c049 as a proposed consequence of the potential and conventions, rather than an assumed scale hierarchy.

claims.title: Acceleration-length coordinate derivative
claims.explanation: Differentiate the adopted inverse coordinate map at fixed c: d(c^2/Ls)/dLs=-c^2/Ls^2. This is the scalar coefficient of the source's delta kappa relation, not a derivation of a gravitational response.

claims.title: Length coefficient of the adopted null response
claims.explanation: Multiply the equation-(14) density coefficient c^2/(8*pi*G) by the coordinate derivative -c^2/Ls^2. This proposes only the local coefficient in the first line of equation (15); the integral one-form and its canonical justification remain outside this scalar equality.

claims.title: Transformed null-response coefficient equals minus pressure
claims.explanation: Compare the differentiated canonical input with the separately adopted equation-(6) pressure formula. Both coefficients reduce to -c^4/(8*pi*G*Ls^2). Coverage is limited to the coefficient multiplying the area measure and delta Ls in equation (15).

claims.title: Potential force and uniform-cut pressure agree
claims.explanation: Differentiating U with respect to independent Ls gives FL=A*c^4/(8*pi*G*Ls^2), equal to A times the independently stated pressure formula. This establishes the uniform-cut scalar equality, not the nonuniform surface integral.

claims.title: Stationary stress variation has the adopted acceleration coefficient
claims.explanation: Rewrite the adopted stress in the independent acceleration-source chart using Ls=c^2/kappa_src, then differentiate at fixed A. The result A*c^2/(8*pi*G) matches the uniform stationary equation-(14) coefficient per unit duration. This is a coordinate-coefficient comparison, not an equality of field-space integrals.

claims.title: Stationary boost rate in length coordinates
claims.explanation: Substitute kappa=c^2/Ls into the independently adopted stationary rate omega=kappa/c, yielding c/Ls.

claims.title: Matched corner charge times rate equals the potential
claims.explanation: Multiplying A*c^3/(8*pi*G) by kappa/c and substituting the acceleration-length definition gives c^4*A/(8*pi*G*Ls), the separately adopted potential. This compares normalized formulas; it does not establish a complete Hamiltonian variation.

claims.title: Potential-length product and boost charge
claims.explanation: Cancel nonzero Ls in the adopted potential-length product and compare it with c times the separately normalized charge. Both expressions give A*c^4/(8*pi*G). No identification of an arbitrary boost rate with physical evolution is used.

claims.title: Fixed-duration boost-angle derivative
claims.explanation: At fixed stationary duration, differentiate eta=c*dt/Ls. The derivative is -c*dt/Ls^2, the coefficient of delta Ls in equation (20).

claims.title: Corner response per duration in length coordinates
claims.explanation: Multiply the boost-angle derivative by Jeta/dt. The fixed nonzero duration cancels, leaving -c*Jeta/Ls^2. This is the scalar coefficient in the first equality of equation (21).

claims.title: Matched corner response equals minus the potential force
claims.explanation: Evaluate the corner coefficient as -A*c^4/(8*pi*G*Ls^2) and compare it with the negative derivative-defined force. This recovers the equation-(21) scalar length coefficient conditional on the matched corner normalization, orientation, stationary clock and duration.

claims.title: Restricted constant-source action derivative
claims.explanation: Differentiate the primitive obtained from the adopted uniform stationary equation-(14) response after substituting kappa_src=c^2/Ls. The result is -dt*A*c^4/(8*pi*G*Ls^2), equal to -dt*FL from the independent potential derivative. I0 contributes zero. This covers c313 only for the disclosed source-restricted action dependence; it does not derive the full on-shell action or its functional derivative.

claims.title: Area coefficient of ω_s dJ_η = Π_∂ dA
claims.explanation: For c142, differentiate J to obtain ∂J/∂A = c³/(8πG), while Pi = c⁴/(8πG Lk). Substitution of omega = κ/c and κ = c²/Lk makes the left side c⁴/(8πG Lk). Since ∂J/∂A is positive, this coefficient equality also tests the equivalent rate identity omega = c/L_s in c112. J has no Lk dependence, so there is no second coefficient in dJ.

claims.title: Area coefficient of ω_s dJ_η = T dS
claims.explanation: For c143, the independently adopted entropy gives ∂S/∂A = kB c³/(4G hbar). Multiplication by T = hbar c/(2πkB Lk) gives c⁴/(8πG Lk), the same area coefficient as omega·∂J/∂A. Both J and S are independent of Lk.

claims.title: Length coefficient of J_η dω_s = −F_L dL_κ
claims.explanation: For c144, ∂omega/∂Lk = −c/Lk². Multiplication by J gives −Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²). Independently differentiating U with the force convention gives F = Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²). omega is independent of A.

claims.title: Length coefficient of J_η dω_s = S dT
claims.explanation: For c145, differentiating the supplied thermal normalization gives ∂T/∂Lk = −hbar c/(2πkB Lk²). Multiplication by S = kB Ac³/(4G hbar) gives −Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²), equal to J·∂omega/∂Lk. Both T and omega are independent of A.

claims.title: Area coefficient of the positive-branch thermal state law
claims.explanation: This covers the dA coefficient of c264, not the entire differential identity by itself. At fixed Lk, ∂U/∂A = c⁴/(8πG Lk), and T·∂S/∂A has the same value. The −F dLk term has zero dA coefficient because A and Lk are independent.

claims.title: Length coefficient of the positive-branch thermal state law
claims.explanation: This covers the dLk coefficient of c264. The adopted zero-constant entropy depends only on A, so ∂S/∂Lk = 0. Both sides reduce to −Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²). The equality also uses the defining force convention, so this coefficient is not an independent canonical justification of F.

claims.title: Entropy–potential product and equivalent boost-product identities
claims.explanation: Directly tests c265: both sides reduce to Ac³/(4G hbar). Substituting the independently adopted entropy S/kB = 2πJ/hbar and cancelling nonzero factors makes this same equality U Lk = cJ, covering c116 because L_s = Lk. With omega = c/Lk, it is also equivalent to U = J omega in c114. Thus these are algebraically equivalent formulations, not three independent verifications. The numerical equality U Lk/c = J is the scalar part of c266; its physical boost-charge meaning remains separate.

claims.title: Entropy density equals pressure–length divided by temperature
claims.explanation: For c267, P = c⁴/(8πG Lk²) gives P Lk/T = kB c³/(4G hbar). Independently, the adopted entropy gives S/A = kB c³/(4G hbar). The division by T is valid on the stated positive branch.

claims.title: Entropy density in Planck-area units
claims.explanation: For c268, substituting ellP2 = G hbar/c³ makes the right side kB c³/(4G hbar), equal to S/A from the adopted entropy. This compares two disclosed normalizations; it is not an independent derivation of Einstein entropy.

claims.title: Direct coefficient of Π_∂ dA = T dS
claims.explanation: Directly records c307 rather than relying only on two comparisons with omega dJ. Pi and T·∂S/∂A each reduce to c⁴/(8πG Lk); the Lk coefficient of dS vanishes. This shares the same area coefficient as g03_firstlaw_area and is not independent evidence.

claims.title: Direct coefficient of −F_L dL_κ = S dT
claims.explanation: Directly tests c308. The force derivative and the independently normalized entropy–temperature product both give −Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²). The minus sign is preserved; T has no A dependence.

claims.title: Direct response-density equality and normalization factor
claims.explanation: Directly tests c316 without using S on either side. Substitution gives [c⁴/(8πG Lk)]·[2πkB Lk/(hbar c)] = kB c³/(4G hbar). The numeric factor is 2π/(8π) = 1/4, covering the scalar cancellation underlying c270. This does not derive either physical normalization.

claims.title: Acceleration length from the supplied surface gravity
claims.explanation: Substitute the adopted kappa=c^2/(2 R_H) into the independently defined acceleration length c^2/kappa. The resulting cancellation gives 2 R_H; that family length relation is not assumed.

claims.title: Length force after independent differentiation
claims.explanation: First evaluate -partial U/partial L_s=c^4 A/(8 pi G L_s^2) at independent A and L_s. Only then substitute A_H and L_k. The radius and pi factors cancel, giving c^4/(8 G).

claims.title: Boundary potential and Schwarzschild mass energy
claims.explanation: The substituted potential gives U_H=c^4 R_H/(4 G). Compare this with M c^2/2 using the explicitly adopted inferred mass–radius compatibility. Since E is defined as M c^2, this also expresses c149's equivalent relation E=2 U_H.

claims.title: Mass-based radial force versus the length force
claims.explanation: Compare the separately stated F_R=M kappa with twice the independently differentiated and then restricted F_L. Both expressions reduce to c^4/(4 G); F_R=2 F_L is not a defining premise.

claims.title: Transformed radial pressure
claims.explanation: Compare P_R=F_R/A_H with twice the restricted normal-scale density F_L/A. Their common expression is c^4/(16 pi G R_H^2). This is a density conversion within the adopted family, not an additional pressure degree of freedom.

claims.title: Length-to-radius work coefficient
claims.explanation: Translate F_L dL_k=F_R dR_H into its coefficient along independent R_H. Differentiate the derived L_k=c^2/kappa to obtain dL_k/dR_H=2, then compare with the independently stated mass-based F_R. This is not a definition of F_R.

claims.title: Radius-to-volume work coefficient
claims.explanation: Differentiate V_H=4 pi R_H^3/3 to obtain 4 pi R_H^2=A_H, covering c188's ordinary volume coefficient. Multiplication by P_R=F_R/A_H then gives F_R. Because the adopted comparison formula is F_R=M kappa, the same equality is the abstract's c186 coefficient M kappa=P_R dV_H/dR_H.

claims.title: Boundary-energy slope along the radius family
claims.explanation: Differentiate the restricted potential, rather than an independently variable area potential at fixed area. Both dU_H/dR_H and P_R dV_H/dR_H reduce to c^4/(4 G). This covers the ordinary family coefficient of dU_H=P_R dV_H.

claims.title: Integrated radial-pressure identity
claims.explanation: Substitute the independently specified potential, radial density and areal volume; both sides give c^4 R_H/(4 G). Since 3 V_H/A_H=R_H, this equality is also U_H=F_R R_H, equivalent to c179's F_R=U_H/R_H on R_H>0.

claims.title: Mass-energy and doubled length-work coefficients
claims.explanation: Using the disclosed mass–radius compatibility, dE/dR_H=c^4/(2 G). Independently, the right side uses the partial-derivative force followed by family restriction and the radius derivative of L_k, giving the same coefficient. This translates dE=2 F_L dL_k only within the stated family.

claims.title: Thermal product from the separate temperature and entropy dictionary
claims.explanation: Multiply the separately adopted Hawking temperature and zero-constant Einstein entropy. hbar and kB cancel, leaving T S=kappa A_H c^2/(8 pi G)=c^4 R_H/(4 G). Compare with M c^2/2 using the disclosed mass–radius premise; TS=U_H was not assumed.

claims.title: Stated Schwarzschild Smarr product balance
claims.explanation: Compute the two products from the separate thermal dictionary and the independently differentiated mechanical potential. Each gives c^4 R_H/(4 G), and their sum equals E=c^4 R_H/(2 G). This is the stated family product identity, not a derivation of the Hamiltonian first law.

claims.title: CK force from differentiation before family restriction
claims.explanation: The defining computation is −∂U_base/∂L_s = c⁴A/(8πG L_s²), followed by A = 4πR_A² and L_s = R_A. This proposes the force formula of Eq. (32), not its canonical physical justification.

claims.title: CK normal-pressure coefficient
claims.explanation: Compare the derivative-defined force divided by spherical area with the separately printed pressure formula. The expanded calculation divides c⁴/(2G) by 4πR_A².

claims.title: Screen pressure and adopted bulk energy density
claims.explanation: The adopted matter relation gives ρ = [c⁴R_A/(2G)]/[4πR_A³/3] = 3c⁴/(8πG R_A²). Compare one third of that expression with the independently derivative-defined screen pressure. This does not derive the Einstein matter–geometry input.

claims.title: Restricted boundary potential and geometric horizon energy
claims.explanation: Compare the independently adopted geometric energy with U_base evaluated at A = 4πR_A² and L_s = R_A. The restricted potential becomes c⁴R_A/(2G); equality to E_A was not used to define U_CK.

claims.title: Force-length product
claims.explanation: Compare E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G) with the derivative-defined force multiplied by the separately assigned L_CK = R_A. This covers the mechanical product in Eq. (33), not its thermal product.

claims.title: Integrated pressure-volume identity
claims.explanation: Compare the geometric energy with 3[c⁴/(8πG R_A²)][4πR_A³/3]. This is a pointwise identity on the specified spherical CK family, not an assertion of an independently stored pressure energy.

claims.title: CK length-to-radius work Jacobian
claims.explanation: Evaluate the defining work-coordinate transformation F_R = F_L(dL_CK/dR_A). The adopted family relation L_CK = R_A gives dL_CK/dR_A = 1. This covers the scalar coefficient content of coincident length and radius work.

claims.title: CK force and energy mass equivalent
claims.explanation: Compare the derivative-defined force with [E_A/c²][c²/R_A] = E_A/R_A = c⁴/(2G). The mass equivalent uses E_A, not an independent material mass.

claims.title: Radius pressure equals normal and screen pressure
claims.explanation: Compare F_R/A_A with F_L/A_A after evaluating the length-to-radius Jacobian. Since P_scr is the disclosed alias of P_L_CK, this also covers the printed equality P_R = P_scr, without adding a separate tautological alias claim.

claims.title: Ordinary radial coefficient of the CK screen-state law
claims.explanation: Translate dE_A = Π_CK dA_A − P_scr dV_A into its R_A coefficient. The expanded quantities are E_A' = c⁴/(2G), A_A' = 8πR_A, V_A' = 4πR_A² and Π_CK = c⁴/(8πG R_A); the proposed right side is c⁴/G − c⁴/(2G). This is only the ordinary mechanical family coefficient.

claims.title: Total energy slope along the spherical CK family
claims.explanation: Express dE_A/dV_A = P_scr without a derivative denominator: E_A' = P_scr V_A'. Here V_A' = 4πR_A² is positive, so this coefficient comparison is equivalent to the stated total slope. Both sides expand to c⁴/(2G); no fixed-entropy partial derivative is introduced.

claims.title: CK pressure representation of the inverse-radius scale
claims.explanation: Compare R_A⁻² with [8πG/c⁴][c⁴/(8πG R_A²)]. This covers only the pressure-to-radius equality in Eq. (35), not its Hubble-rate or spatial-curvature expressions and not Friedmann dynamics.

consequences.title: Mechanical differential as two scalar coefficients
consequences.text: Conditional on the proposed translation being faithful and the two derivative equalities holding, the independent-coordinate law is dU_b=Pi_b dA−F_L dL_s. This follows from the evaluated coefficients and the adopted response definitions, without any horizon-family constraint.

consequences.title: Common-potential product identities
consequences.text: The proposed ratio checks, together with P_L=F_L/A, give U_b=Pi_b A=F_L L_s=P_L A L_s. They are different algebraic expressions of the same specified potential, not evidence for separately stored energies.

consequences.title: Stress slope along the length coordinate
consequences.text: The proposed length-slope check identifies P_L with minus the L_s derivative of Pi_b at fixed A. Multiplying by A gives A∂Pi_b/∂L_s=−F_L. This concerns changes between boundary configurations, not a spatial gradient inside a material layer.

consequences.title: Scale laws and the mass-equivalent identity remain conditional
consequences.text: With the adopted coordinate, coupling and mass conventions, the proposed checks yield 1/L_s=κ_E Pi_b, 1/L_s²=κ_E P_L and F_L=M_b κ. These are scalar consequences of the selected potential; they do not independently establish canonical dynamics or a material force law.

consequences.title: Conditional length-pressure coefficient
consequences.text: If the proposed translation is faithful and equation (14) is accepted as input, its length-coordinate density coefficient is minus the adopted pressure. The derivative-defined force agrees with area times that pressure for a uniform cut.

consequences.title: Stationary stress coefficient comparison
consequences.text: The proposed acceleration-chart derivative of the adopted stress matches the uniform canonical coefficient per stationary duration. This comparison does not supply the null-action derivation.

consequences.title: Complementary stationary corner calculation
consequences.text: With the shared clock, area normalization and orientation, the charge-rate product reproduces the potential, and the fixed-duration corner coefficient reproduces minus the length force. These are conditional scalar identities, not a complete Hamiltonian first law.

consequences.title: Local force versus integrated source derivative
consequences.text: For the disclosed restricted stationary action primitive, the constant-source derivative carries the duration factor: minus dt times FL. Removing that factor requires the local-response interpretation supplied by the physical canonical premise.

consequences.title: Conditional independent-coordinate thermal state law
consequences.text: If the proposed translation is faithful, the two coefficient equalities together express dU = T dS − F dLk on the stated independent-coordinate positive branch. They do not establish a covariant moving-horizon first law.

consequences.title: Two complementary derivative directions
consequences.text: The area direction has coefficient c⁴/(8πG Lk); the length direction has coefficient −Ac⁴/(8πG Lk²). The boost and thermal descriptions reproduce these same respective coefficients under their separately adopted normalizations.

consequences.title: Equivalent potential and boost products
consequences.text: The entropy-product comparison is equivalent, under the adopted entropy and rate definitions, to U L_s = cJ and U = J omega. These equivalent rewrites are not independent confirmations of the canonical interpretation.

consequences.title: Direct entropy-density chain
consequences.text: The proposed scalar comparisons give S/A = P Lk/T = kB/(4ellP2). The response-to-Planck equality does not require entropy as an intermediate expression, but still requires the supplied temperature and Planck-area definitions.

consequences.title: Numerical quarter from supplied coefficients
consequences.text: Within the adopted dictionary, dividing the mechanical coefficient by temperature cancels the length and yields the factor 2π/(8π) = 1/4. This is a conditional normalization calculation, not a derivation of regular-state thermality.

consequences.title: Conditional agreement of work coordinates
consequences.text: If the proposed coefficient equalities hold under the disclosed premises, length work, radius work and radial-pressure volume work agree along the Schwarzschild family. The corresponding expressions are F_L=c^4/(8 G), F_R=c^4/(4 G) and P_R=c^4/(16 pi G R_H^2).

consequences.title: Boundary-energy and mass-energy variations are not independent additions
consequences.text: The proposed equalities imply E=2 U_H and dU_H/dR_H=F_L restricted to the family times dL_k/dR_H. The mass-energy coefficient is twice this boundary-energy coefficient. These are relations within one constrained family, not evidence for separately stored energies or an extra term to append to the mass first law.

consequences.title: Coincident thermal and force-length products
consequences.text: Together, the proposed thermal-product and Smarr equalities imply TS=F_L L_k=E/2=U_H on this family. Their coincidence depends on the adopted thermal normalization, entropy convention and mass–radius compatibility; it does not establish those physical inputs.

consequences.title: Conditional screen energy and pressure identifications
consequences.text: If the proposed translation is faithful, these candidate comparisons express U_∂ = E_A and P_scr = ρ/3 for the separately assigned CK family. The Einstein matter–geometry relation remains an adopted premise.

consequences.title: Conditional coincidence of scalar work coordinates
consequences.text: The adopted relation L_CK = R_A gives a unit work-coordinate Jacobian. The proposed comparisons therefore identify radius force with length force and radius pressure with the normal-pressure coefficient, whose screen notation is P_scr.

consequences.title: One-dimensional screen-state coefficients
consequences.text: The proposed family-law and slope comparisons concern ordinary derivatives in R_A. They do not identify this total slope with a fixed-entropy partial derivative or with bulk material pressure.

consequences.title: Scale identity without a dynamics derivation
consequences.text: Conditional on the adopted definitions, the inverse-radius comparison represents the horizon scale using screen pressure. It supplies no derivation of Einstein–Friedmann evolution.

extractionWarnings: PDF text order, symbols, superscripts and equation layout can be imperfect. Numbered lines are an extraction index; compare the original PDF before approval. The AI also receives the original PDF for equation reading.
This is a fresh private proposed-formulation inventory. Author approval and publication consent are not recorded; no claim is marked verified or approved.

Only the supplied numbered extraction and layout-preserving parsed text were accessible here; an independent visual inspection of the original PDF binary was not possible. Equation readings require author inspection against that PDF.

The extracted two-column order interleaves unrelated expressions. Superscript, subscript, numerator and denominator rows have been attached to their associated claims; comma-like κ , 0 and δκ , 0 are interpreted contextually as nonzero conditions, pending PDF confirmation.
The groups are partial scalar-check proposals, not proofs of the paper. Their conclusions would be conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the source.

The canonical gravitational response, selected action, orientation, clock conversion and endpoints require justification independent of differentiating U_∂. The companion Appendix I and its reported checks were not supplied.
Tensor geometry, null-boundary variational calculus, functional derivatives, integrals, exterior forms, causal classifications and cosmological solutions remain outside the stated scalar AST.
The FRW square-root radius formula is preserved as stated. A squared scalar consequence would not prove the original positive branch or its domain.
Independent (A,L_s) mechanics and thermal translation are separated from constrained Schwarzschild and CK radius families. Family substitution must not precede the defining partial derivatives.

The conclusion's statement that κ is regular at zero does not make L_s = c²/κ regular there. Extension through zero, including the Hayward radiation limit, needs a separate chart or limiting prescription.

The signed de Sitter convention needs care: the source uses a positive-magnitude length, whereas the general mechanics uses signed L_s. The positive thermal branch must not be imposed silently on a signed cosmological rate.
Table 2 uses k in θ+2k without defining it locally; it must not be confused with FRW spatial-curvature k.
The Hayward work identity contains an independent dw term. The fixed-variable meaning of its radial response and its distinction from work density need author confirmation.
The radiation and de Sitter Hayward specializations need explicit equation-of-state premises for scalar checks. Ong's quoted E=M/2 comparison also leaves its units implicit.

The source states that no observational data are used. No observational validation or empirical prediction is established by these identities; the manuscript's physical applicability and novelty remain separate review questions.

No external citation, archived review, companion implementation or saved check result was independently read or validated. Reference [23] does not establish acceptance, approval or verification in this review.
No literal source URLs are supplied in the manuscript text; sourceUrl fields are therefore empty rather than synthesized from arXiv identifiers or DOIs.
This remains a fresh private review of a proposed formulation: authorApprovalRecorded=false and publishConsent=false. Nothing here records approval, publication, or verification of the entire paper.
The supplied numbered extraction was compared with the supplied layout-preserving parsed text. No independent visual inspection of the original PDF binary or external companion material was possible.
Both listed missingSourceLineIds, p1-l023 and p1-l025, are accounted for in the complete corrected span of c035. They belong to the opening work-coordinate interpretation, not to metadata.

All 304 existing coverage units are retained. The 16 additions bring the inventory to 320 coverage units; the two inferred inputs bring it to 29 inputs. The updated list contains five mathematical groups.

Each new assertion unit contains at most one equality. Direct equalities added from equation chains are not additional independent proofs. Existing broad interpretations and contextual units are not promoted to checked claims.

The mathematical groups are bounded candidate selections, not exhaustive proof assignments. Retained coverage outside their named targets—including general work-form identities, geometric normalization details, cosmological dynamics, Hayward reconstruction and some thermal family products—remains visible but unassessed by those selections.

Any scientific conclusion from a scalar check would be conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the manuscript and on its stated physical inputs. Restating a derivative definition, assigned rate, entropy law or already assumed family value is not an independent proof.

The canonical action response, clock conversion, orientation, endpoints and retained other sectors require gravitational justification independent of differentiating U_∂. Functional, integral, tensor and exterior-form claims remain unsupported by ordinary scalar algebra; the companion Appendix I was not supplied.

Input i22 records the manuscript's asserted Friedmann representation; it is not an independent proof of the same equations. In particular, c234, c235, c311 and c312 must not be certified by assuming those very displayed relations as premises.

The general mass-first-law foundation in c137 remains distinct from the ordinary Schwarzschild family coefficient comparison in c150. Neither the product rule nor family integrability authorizes adding a second scale-work term to the mass variation.

The radiation and de Sitter equation-of-state premises i28 and i29 are inferred from named specializations, not separately printed or independently established. At radiation the signed Hayward rate vanishes, so its nonzero length-coordinate chart and equation (39) cannot simply be evaluated there.

The signed acceleration-length chart excludes κ=0. The conclusion's statement about regular κ does not extend L_s=c²/κ through zero. Positive-magnitude de Sitter lengths and positive-temperature formulas must not silently replace signed rate conventions.

The Hayward work identity retains its dw term. Its radial coefficient requires the stated variable convention, and its signed radial response must remain distinct from both the quadratic normal response and Hayward work density.

The original FRW square-root formula requires its real positive branch; a squared scalar rewrite does not prove that branch. Areal volume is not generally proper spatial volume for nonzero curvature, and individual marginal cuts do not establish a null nonexpanding worldtube.
Table 2's k in θ+2k remains locally undefined and must not be identified with FRW curvature k. Ong's quoted E=M/2 also leaves its unit convention implicit.

The source states that no observational data are used. The inventory establishes no observational validation or empirical prediction; this statement does not settle physical applicability or historical novelty.

No cited paper, archived review, external implementation or saved check result was independently examined. The manuscript's reference to an earlier review supplies no approval or verification evidence for this fresh review.

limitations: This checks exact scalar mathematical identities and dimensions under the listed definitions and symbol domains; it is not a Lean proof or experimental validation.
Prose assumptions, source citations, novelty, explanatory importance, tensor equations, and general physical interpretations are not verified automatically.
A nonzero residual means the equality is not an identity on the declared domain; it may hold at particular values.

explanation.title: The proposal and the scope of this review
explanation.text:
The central idea is to express a specified gravitational boundary potential using an acceleration length, L_s = c²/κ. The length is signed; its magnitude is L_κ = |L_s|, and the coordinate chart excludes κ = 0. The manuscript motivates its geometric normalization through a uniformly accelerated Rindler observer and the observer’s instantaneous rest slice. It does not identify this length with every horizon’s radius or with a photon travel distance.

The adopted potential is U_∂ = Aκc²/(8πG). The checker confirms its rewrite as U_∂ = c⁴A/(8πG L_s). Area and length are treated as independent coordinates before imposing a particular horizon family.

This is a fresh private review of a proposed translation: author approval and publication consent are not recorded. The supplied SymPy report marks all 60 selected scalar equalities checked, with zero residuals, consistent dimensions and established mathematical domain restrictions. Scientific conclusions remain conditional on faithful translation and the stated physical inputs. This is not verification of the whole manuscript or of its claim to a new interpretation.

explanation.title: What follows from the common potential
explanation.text:
Differentiating the adopted potential gives dU_∂ = Π_∂ dA − F_L dL_s, where Π_∂ = c⁴/(8πG L_s), F_L = Ac⁴/(8πG L_s²), and P_L = F_L/A = c⁴/(8πG L_s²) = κ²/(8πG). These selected derivative and coefficient comparisons are checked. Thus the pressure density is positive on either nonzero signed-length branch, while the potential and area stress follow the sign of L_s.

The checked ratio identities imply U_∂ = Π_∂A = F_LL_s = P_LAL_s. With the adopted mass equivalent M_∂ = U_∂/c², they also give F_L = M_∂κ. This is an identity between boundary-response quantities, not a material acceleration law. The scale relations 1/L_s = κ_EΠ_∂ and 1/L_s² = κ_EP_L follow using κ_E = 8πG/c⁴. At fixed area, the checked slope is ∂Π_∂/∂L_s = −P_L: it concerns nearby boundary configurations, not a gradient through matter. The additional zero-area coefficient needed for the full stress differential was not separately submitted.

No enclosed volume is needed. The manuscript introduces A dL_s as a work one-form and argues, using its exterior derivative, that it is not a global volume differential on the independent-coordinate space. That exterior-calculus argument is NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL. For spherical volume work the displacement is instead dR, so the conjugate pressure must be transformed; AL_s is not generally the sphere’s volume.

explanation.title: The supplied canonical argument and the checked coefficient
explanation.text:
The manuscript supplies a canonical argument beyond differentiating a chosen energy. It adopts the cited null scalar source μ = κ̂ + θ/2, exchanges the area and rate polarizations, and restricts to nonexpanding boundaries and tangent variations, θ = δθ = 0. Nullness is preserved, other responses are controlled rather than discarded, and the clock, cuts and interval are prescribed. A null generator is not assigned material proper acceleration or proper time.

After conversion to acceleration units and physical time, equation (14) supplies the response coefficient c²/(8πG) multiplying δκ and the area and time measures. This gravitational response is an adopted input to the scalar checker. What is checked is the coordinate change: ∂κ/∂L_s = −c²/L_s², so the transformed coefficient is −c⁴/(8πG L_s²) = −P_L. The uniform-cut comparison F_L = AP_L also checks.

The source additionally describes a companion Appendix I deriving the Einstein–Hilbert current from metric and variation data in fixed Gaussian-null gauge, using I_rate = I_EH − B_0 + B_μ and a specified endpoint shift. It states that tangent nonexpansion controls the endpoint area variations. This is a reported restricted local derivation, not an absent argument. The companion calculation, endpoint reasoning, polarization integrals and full canonical identification are NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL; only the downstream scalar coefficients were reproduced.

explanation.title: The stationary boost comparison and the duration factor
explanation.text:
The complementary stationary construction adopts a matched area–boost coefficient J_η = Ac³/(8πG), rate ω_s = κ/c and corner orientation. The checked scalar comparisons give ω_s = c/L_s, U_∂ = J_ηω_s and U_∂L_s = cJ_η. At fixed duration Δτ, the adopted relation η = cΔτ/L_s yields (J_η/Δτ)∂η/∂L_s = −cJ_η/L_s² = −F_L. A separate checked acceleration-source derivative of the stated stress also matches the adopted uniform response coefficient.

The action check has a narrower meaning. The proposed model integrates equation (14) at fixed area and controlled other data to a restricted primitive I0 + Δτ A[c²/(8πG)]κ. After replacing κ by c²/L_s, its checked derivative is −ΔτF_L. The factor of duration is essential: an integrated constant-source derivative is not the local force itself. This primitive does not supply the complete physical on-shell action or establish its functional Hamilton–Jacobi derivative.

The manuscript explicitly warns that source-dependent action additions can shift the response, that arbitrary-source existence is not asserted, and that the selected corner one-form is not a complete Hamiltonian variation. Its field-space two-form and one-pair interpretation remain outside these scalar checks.

explanation.title: Schwarzschild: why radius pressure is twice length pressure
explanation.text:
For the supplied Schwarzschild family, the clock is normalized at infinity, A_H = 4πR_H² and κ = c²/(2R_H). These geometric relations are inputs, not consequences of the boundary potential. The model also discloses the inferred mass–radius compatibility Mc² = c⁴R_H/(2G), which needs confirmation as part of the proposed translation.

The checked calculations give L_κ = 2R_H, F_L = c⁴/(8G) and U_∂ = Mc²/2. The model adopts F_R = Mκ as a comparison formula; the checks establish its agreement with transformed length work: F_R = F_L(dL_κ/dR_H) = 2F_L. Consequently P_R = 2P_L, with the evaluated radial density c⁴/(16πG R_H²).

Using the adopted areal volume V_H = 4πR_H³/3, the checked coefficient comparisons give F_L dL_κ = F_R dR_H = P_R dV_H and therefore the abstract’s Mκ dR_H = P_R dV_H. The boundary-energy slope and integrated identity also check: dU_∂ = P_R dV_H and U_∂ = 3P_RV_H. The factor of two comes from changing the work coordinate; it is not another pressure degree of freedom. The source interprets this as horizon-size change, not motion of a second surface at 2R_H. Preservation of the full canonical response still depends on the prior action prescription.

explanation.title: Boundary energy is not an extra term in the mass first law
explanation.text:
The Schwarzschild comparisons distinguish the boundary potential from mass energy E = Mc². The checked potential relation gives E = 2U_∂. With the separately adopted temperature and zero-constant Einstein entropy, the thermal product checks as TS = E/2. The checked Smarr product balance E = TS + F_LL_κ then implies TS = F_LL_κ = U_∂. These are conditional consequences of shared formulas, not independent energy stores.

The checked radius coefficients give dE = 2F_L dL_κ. Combining the checked boundary-energy slope with the work-coordinate comparisons also yields dU_∂ = F_L dL_κ along this family; that last equality was not a separately submitted target.

The source’s broader argument is that a mass first law is a Hamiltonian variation with its symplectic-potential subtraction and possible generator corrections, not merely the full differential of Aκ. It accordingly warns against appending scale work as an independent addition to dE = T dS. The Hamiltonian foundation was not reproduced here. Several displayed family differential identities—including dE = T dS and the full thermal form of equation (28)—also remain without separate checker targets. Their untested status does not establish an error in them.

explanation.title: The separately assigned Cai–Kim cosmological screen
explanation.text:
The FRW application has different physical premises from the stationary null-action construction. For a spherical marginal horizon it adopts A_A = 4πR_A², geometric energy E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G), and the Einstein matter–geometry relation E_A = ρV_A, with V_A = 4πR_A³/3. This is areal volume, not generally proper spatial volume. The instantaneous Cai–Kim prescription separately assigns κ_CK = c²/R_A and L_CK = R_A; marginal cuts alone do not make the evolving worldtube null and nonexpanding.

After the independent-coordinate derivatives are taken, the checked family substitutions give F_L = c⁴/(2G), P_scr = c⁴/(8πG R_A²) = ρ/3 and U_∂ = E_A. The density equality requires the adopted Einstein input; defining pressure does not derive that input. The products E_A = F_LL_CK = 3P_scrV_A and the mass-equivalent comparison F_L = M_Aκ_CK also check.

Because L_CK = R_A, the work-coordinate Jacobian is one, so the selected comparisons give F_R = F_L and P_R = P_L = P_scr, unlike Schwarzschild’s factor of two. The ordinary radius coefficient of dE_A = Π_CK dA_A − P_scr dV_A checks, as do dE_A/dV_A = P_scr and 1/R_A² = κ_EP_scr. This is a constrained total slope, not a fixed-entropy pressure derivative or an identification with bulk material pressure. The manuscript distinguishes this screen-state bookkeeping from matter supply across a momentarily fixed horizon and explicitly does not infer exact equilibrium thermality for arbitrary FRW evolution.

explanation.title: Thermal translation requires an additional physical dictionary
explanation.text:
Temperature and entropy are not obtained from the mechanical potential alone. The source separately invokes a regular Hawking–Unruh/KMS state, the Euclidean period cΔτ_E = 2πL_κ, the temperature k_BT = ℏ|κ|/(2πc), and Einstein entropy with zero additive constant, S/k_B = 2πJ_η/ℏ. Their physical foundations are inputs to these checks.

On the specified positive branch, the checked derivative coefficients identify the area contribution as ω_s dJ_η = Π_∂ dA = T dS and the length contribution as J_η dω_s = −F_L dL_κ = S dT. Both coefficients of the independent-coordinate law dU_∂ = T dS − F_L dL_κ check. The length coefficient partly restates the adopted force definition; these comparisons are not independent canonical proofs.

The checked product comparison gives S/k_B = 2πU_∂L_κ/(ℏc), equivalent under the adopted dictionary to U_∂L_κ = cJ_η. The density comparisons give S/A = P_LL_κ/T = k_B/(4ℓ_P²). Dividing the supplied mechanical coefficient by the supplied temperature cancels the length and produces the numerical factor 2π/(8π) = 1/4. This explains consistency between the normalizations, not a derivation of Hawking thermality or Einstein entropy. The boost-charge interpretation still relies on the cited canonical foundation.

explanation.title: Further source results that remain unverified here
explanation.text:
The manuscript goes beyond the selected checks by rewriting Friedmann acceleration and conservation in screen-pressure variables and interpreting a two-dimensional normal Ricci scalar. Apart from the pressure-to-radius identity already discussed, these dynamical and geometric assertions are NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL. They require Einstein–Friedmann dynamics and the stated metric conventions, not merely the definition of pressure.

The signed Hayward comparison is also unverified context. The source states κ_H^s/κ_CK = (3w−1)/4, a quadratic normal response P_L^H = (P_scr−p_m)²/(16P_scr), and a scale-work identity containing both a volume term and −(3/4)E_A dw. The dw term must remain when w varies. Its signed radial response is distinguished from both the quadratic normal response and Hayward work density; reconstructing material pressure is presented as an on-shell relation, not a new equation of state.

The proposed translation exposes w = 1/3 and w = −1 as inferred premises for the named radiation and de Sitter specializations. They need confirmation. The source’s radiation example reaches zero signed Hayward rate, where a nonzero acceleration-length chart cannot simply be evaluated. The CK thermal products and thermal family differential likewise have no dedicated checks in this report. These are limits of coverage, not findings that the source results are false. Moving-boundary and higher-curvature extensions are explicitly assigned separate derivations.

explanation.title: Limits of the conclusions
explanation.text:
The report establishes exact identities only for the submitted scalar expressions under their declared definitions and domains. The five models were checked separately; physical compatibility between regimes was not established automatically. Repeated product identities and equivalent coefficient comparisons should not be counted as independent physical evidence.

Source fidelity remains a separate task. The supplied extraction interleaves columns and separates equation superscripts and denominators; the original PDF layout needs inspection. The FRW square-root radius and its positive-radicand branch are not represented by the independent-radius checks. Likewise, the conclusion’s statement that κ is regular at zero does not extend L_s = c²/κ through zero.

The source reports a companion implementation and saved results, but those materials and the cited papers were not independently examined here. The earlier review cited by the manuscript provides no evidence for this fresh assessment. NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL does not mean NOT PRESENT IN THE MANUSCRIPT. No contradiction was reported for the tested expressions, and uncovered material is not thereby erroneous.
