review.summary: This private diagnostic review finds strong bounded algebraic consistency in the proposed formulation. The supplied SymPy report checks all 60 selected scalar equalities with zero residuals, consistent dimensions and established mathematical domain restrictions. Conditional on faithful translation, these support the common-potential mechanics, the selected null-response and stationary-corner coefficient comparisons, Schwarzschild work-coordinate identities, positive-branch thermal translations, and assigned Cai–Kim screen identities. They do not verify the entire manuscript, its physical premises, references, historical contribution or broader extensions. Author approval and publication consent are not recorded.
review.explanatoryContribution: The useful organizing idea is to express the specified boundary potential in acceleration-length coordinates and distinguish its area response from its length response. This makes the difference between normal-scale pressure and radius-work pressure transparent: the Schwarzschild family has a factor-two coordinate Jacobian, while the assigned Cai–Kim family has a unit Jacobian. The manuscript also separates boundary-potential bookkeeping from the Hamiltonian mass first law and introduces thermal quantities as additional physical inputs. Whether this coordinate-based interpretation adds substantive physical insight beyond its cited canonical antecedents requires specialist and historical assessment; algebra alone does not establish novelty.
review.correctness: 60/60 selected mathematical candidates returned checked. 71 source coverage units remain unresolved. Definition restatements are not independent derivations. No mathematical contradiction is reported for the exact submitted expressions on their declared domains. The checks correctly preserve differentiation before family substitution and include denominator, substitution-domain and dimensional audits. Their force is conditional: the potential, several canonical coefficients, family geometry, mass–radius compatibility, temperature and entropy are adopted or inferred inputs. The restricted action primitive is not the full on-shell action, and its checked ordinary derivative is not a verification of the functional Hamilton–Jacobi relation. Some broader coverage units remain unresolved despite checked subcoefficients or consequences. Several comparisons are algebraically equivalent, so their number should not be interpreted as independent confirmation. PDF-to-formulation fidelity remains to be assessed.
review.physicalJustification: The listed physical inputs are adopted premises, not established by these algebraic checks. The manuscript does supply a physical justification program: cited null scalar canonical data, a polarization exchange, tangent nonexpanding variations, physical-clock conversion, a selected rate action with endpoint conditions, and a complementary stationary area–boost construction. It also describes a restricted Gaussian-null Einstein–Hilbert derivation in companion Appendix I. These arguments are not absent; they were not reproduced by this scalar pipeline. Further assessment should inspect that derivation and its gauge, orientation, clock, endpoint and controlled-sector assumptions, then establish the claimed action-response identification within the stated prescription. Rindler normalization, Schwarzschild geometry, Misner–Sharp/Einstein matter identification and the separate CK calibration likewise need their own geometric and physical assessment. The thermal interpretation depends on the cited regular-state normalization and adopted Einstein entropy, not on mechanics alone. The relevant independent foundations are invoked through source citations but were not independently evaluated here. No new experiment is inherently required for the conditional GR identities; any claimed empirical realization would require a specified observable, applicable state or regime, and relevant evidence.
review.priorWork: No literature-wide novelty search or independent source verification was performed by this pipeline. The source explicitly identifies Parattu–Majhi–Padmanabhan [5], Hopfmüller–Freidel [8,9] and Odak–Rignon-Bret–Speziale [10] as canonical antecedents, and Carlip–Teitelboim [11] and Bianchi–Wieland [12] for the area–boost route. Its cosmological inputs and comparisons cite Cai–Kim [14], Misner–Sharp [15], Hayward [16,22], Faraoni [17], Kong [18] and Ong [21]; its thermal dictionary cites Unruh [7], Hawking [19] and Gibbons–Hawking [20]. These are the manuscript’s attributions, not independently validated readings. Its qualified priority claim is appropriate to retain as qualified. The earlier review [23] is not evidence for this fresh review.
strengths: The manuscript explicitly separates conditional algebra, canonical justification, geometric normalization and the additional thermal dictionary.
Independent-coordinate differentiation is distinguished from constrained horizon-family variation, preventing a common source of force-coefficient confusion.
The selected nonexpanding-null result is restricted by clock, boundary data, orientation and variation conditions rather than presented as a universal moving-horizon theorem.
The checked Schwarzschild and Cai–Kim examples clearly illustrate how changing the work coordinate changes the conjugate pressure.
Prescription dependence, the distinction from material pressure, and the limits of exact cosmological thermality are acknowledged in the source.
The proposed translation exposes inferred premises and preserves substantial unverified source material instead of treating lack of scalar coverage as a disproof.
openQuestions: Does inspection of the original PDF confirm every reconstructed equation, sign, superscript and fraction, and does the author accept the proposed scalar domains and inferred premises?
Does companion Appendix I establish the stated physical-clock response, endpoint treatment and retained other-sector contributions for exactly the selected action and admissible variations?

contributions.title: The proposal and the scope of this review
contributions.text:
The central idea is to express a specified gravitational boundary potential using an acceleration length, L_s = c²/κ. The length is signed; its magnitude is L_κ = |L_s|, and the coordinate chart excludes κ = 0. The manuscript motivates its geometric normalization through a uniformly accelerated Rindler observer and the observer’s instantaneous rest slice. It does not identify this length with every horizon’s radius or with a photon travel distance.

The adopted potential is U_∂ = Aκc²/(8πG). The checker confirms its rewrite as U_∂ = c⁴A/(8πG L_s). Area and length are treated as independent coordinates before imposing a particular horizon family.

This is a fresh private review of a proposed translation: author approval and publication consent are not recorded. The supplied SymPy report marks all 60 selected scalar equalities checked, with zero residuals, consistent dimensions and established mathematical domain restrictions. Scientific conclusions remain conditional on faithful translation and the stated physical inputs. This is not verification of the whole manuscript or of its claim to a new interpretation.

contributions.title: What follows from the common potential
contributions.text:
Differentiating the adopted potential gives dU_∂ = Π_∂ dA − F_L dL_s, where Π_∂ = c⁴/(8πG L_s), F_L = Ac⁴/(8πG L_s²), and P_L = F_L/A = c⁴/(8πG L_s²) = κ²/(8πG). These selected derivative and coefficient comparisons are checked. Thus the pressure density is positive on either nonzero signed-length branch, while the potential and area stress follow the sign of L_s.

The checked ratio identities imply U_∂ = Π_∂A = F_LL_s = P_LAL_s. With the adopted mass equivalent M_∂ = U_∂/c², they also give F_L = M_∂κ. This is an identity between boundary-response quantities, not a material acceleration law. The scale relations 1/L_s = κ_EΠ_∂ and 1/L_s² = κ_EP_L follow using κ_E = 8πG/c⁴. At fixed area, the checked slope is ∂Π_∂/∂L_s = −P_L: it concerns nearby boundary configurations, not a gradient through matter. The additional zero-area coefficient needed for the full stress differential was not separately submitted.

No enclosed volume is needed. The manuscript introduces A dL_s as a work one-form and argues, using its exterior derivative, that it is not a global volume differential on the independent-coordinate space. That exterior-calculus argument is NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL. For spherical volume work the displacement is instead dR, so the conjugate pressure must be transformed; AL_s is not generally the sphere’s volume.

contributions.title: The supplied canonical argument and the checked coefficient
contributions.text:
The manuscript supplies a canonical argument beyond differentiating a chosen energy. It adopts the cited null scalar source μ = κ̂ + θ/2, exchanges the area and rate polarizations, and restricts to nonexpanding boundaries and tangent variations, θ = δθ = 0. Nullness is preserved, other responses are controlled rather than discarded, and the clock, cuts and interval are prescribed. A null generator is not assigned material proper acceleration or proper time.

After conversion to acceleration units and physical time, equation (14) supplies the response coefficient c²/(8πG) multiplying δκ and the area and time measures. This gravitational response is an adopted input to the scalar checker. What is checked is the coordinate change: ∂κ/∂L_s = −c²/L_s², so the transformed coefficient is −c⁴/(8πG L_s²) = −P_L. The uniform-cut comparison F_L = AP_L also checks.

The source additionally describes a companion Appendix I deriving the Einstein–Hilbert current from metric and variation data in fixed Gaussian-null gauge, using I_rate = I_EH − B_0 + B_μ and a specified endpoint shift. It states that tangent nonexpansion controls the endpoint area variations. This is a reported restricted local derivation, not an absent argument. The companion calculation, endpoint reasoning, polarization integrals and full canonical identification are NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL; only the downstream scalar coefficients were reproduced.

contributions.title: The stationary boost comparison and the duration factor
contributions.text:
The complementary stationary construction adopts a matched area–boost coefficient J_η = Ac³/(8πG), rate ω_s = κ/c and corner orientation. The checked scalar comparisons give ω_s = c/L_s, U_∂ = J_ηω_s and U_∂L_s = cJ_η. At fixed duration Δτ, the adopted relation η = cΔτ/L_s yields (J_η/Δτ)∂η/∂L_s = −cJ_η/L_s² = −F_L. A separate checked acceleration-source derivative of the stated stress also matches the adopted uniform response coefficient.

The action check has a narrower meaning. The proposed model integrates equation (14) at fixed area and controlled other data to a restricted primitive I0 + Δτ A[c²/(8πG)]κ. After replacing κ by c²/L_s, its checked derivative is −ΔτF_L. The factor of duration is essential: an integrated constant-source derivative is not the local force itself. This primitive does not supply the complete physical on-shell action or establish its functional Hamilton–Jacobi derivative.

The manuscript explicitly warns that source-dependent action additions can shift the response, that arbitrary-source existence is not asserted, and that the selected corner one-form is not a complete Hamiltonian variation. Its field-space two-form and one-pair interpretation remain outside these scalar checks.

contributions.title: Schwarzschild: why radius pressure is twice length pressure
contributions.text:
For the supplied Schwarzschild family, the clock is normalized at infinity, A_H = 4πR_H² and κ = c²/(2R_H). These geometric relations are inputs, not consequences of the boundary potential. The model also discloses the inferred mass–radius compatibility Mc² = c⁴R_H/(2G), which needs confirmation as part of the proposed translation.

The checked calculations give L_κ = 2R_H, F_L = c⁴/(8G) and U_∂ = Mc²/2. The model adopts F_R = Mκ as a comparison formula; the checks establish its agreement with transformed length work: F_R = F_L(dL_κ/dR_H) = 2F_L. Consequently P_R = 2P_L, with the evaluated radial density c⁴/(16πG R_H²).

Using the adopted areal volume V_H = 4πR_H³/3, the checked coefficient comparisons give F_L dL_κ = F_R dR_H = P_R dV_H and therefore the abstract’s Mκ dR_H = P_R dV_H. The boundary-energy slope and integrated identity also check: dU_∂ = P_R dV_H and U_∂ = 3P_RV_H. The factor of two comes from changing the work coordinate; it is not another pressure degree of freedom. The source interprets this as horizon-size change, not motion of a second surface at 2R_H. Preservation of the full canonical response still depends on the prior action prescription.

contributions.title: Boundary energy is not an extra term in the mass first law
contributions.text:
The Schwarzschild comparisons distinguish the boundary potential from mass energy E = Mc². The checked potential relation gives E = 2U_∂. With the separately adopted temperature and zero-constant Einstein entropy, the thermal product checks as TS = E/2. The checked Smarr product balance E = TS + F_LL_κ then implies TS = F_LL_κ = U_∂. These are conditional consequences of shared formulas, not independent energy stores.

The checked radius coefficients give dE = 2F_L dL_κ. Combining the checked boundary-energy slope with the work-coordinate comparisons also yields dU_∂ = F_L dL_κ along this family; that last equality was not a separately submitted target.

The source’s broader argument is that a mass first law is a Hamiltonian variation with its symplectic-potential subtraction and possible generator corrections, not merely the full differential of Aκ. It accordingly warns against appending scale work as an independent addition to dE = T dS. The Hamiltonian foundation was not reproduced here. Several displayed family differential identities—including dE = T dS and the full thermal form of equation (28)—also remain without separate checker targets. Their untested status does not establish an error in them.

contributions.title: The separately assigned Cai–Kim cosmological screen
contributions.text:
The FRW application has different physical premises from the stationary null-action construction. For a spherical marginal horizon it adopts A_A = 4πR_A², geometric energy E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G), and the Einstein matter–geometry relation E_A = ρV_A, with V_A = 4πR_A³/3. This is areal volume, not generally proper spatial volume. The instantaneous Cai–Kim prescription separately assigns κ_CK = c²/R_A and L_CK = R_A; marginal cuts alone do not make the evolving worldtube null and nonexpanding.

After the independent-coordinate derivatives are taken, the checked family substitutions give F_L = c⁴/(2G), P_scr = c⁴/(8πG R_A²) = ρ/3 and U_∂ = E_A. The density equality requires the adopted Einstein input; defining pressure does not derive that input. The products E_A = F_LL_CK = 3P_scrV_A and the mass-equivalent comparison F_L = M_Aκ_CK also check.

Because L_CK = R_A, the work-coordinate Jacobian is one, so the selected comparisons give F_R = F_L and P_R = P_L = P_scr, unlike Schwarzschild’s factor of two. The ordinary radius coefficient of dE_A = Π_CK dA_A − P_scr dV_A checks, as do dE_A/dV_A = P_scr and 1/R_A² = κ_EP_scr. This is a constrained total slope, not a fixed-entropy pressure derivative or an identification with bulk material pressure. The manuscript distinguishes this screen-state bookkeeping from matter supply across a momentarily fixed horizon and explicitly does not infer exact equilibrium thermality for arbitrary FRW evolution.

contributions.title: Thermal translation requires an additional physical dictionary
contributions.text:
Temperature and entropy are not obtained from the mechanical potential alone. The source separately invokes a regular Hawking–Unruh/KMS state, the Euclidean period cΔτ_E = 2πL_κ, the temperature k_BT = ℏ|κ|/(2πc), and Einstein entropy with zero additive constant, S/k_B = 2πJ_η/ℏ. Their physical foundations are inputs to these checks.

On the specified positive branch, the checked derivative coefficients identify the area contribution as ω_s dJ_η = Π_∂ dA = T dS and the length contribution as J_η dω_s = −F_L dL_κ = S dT. Both coefficients of the independent-coordinate law dU_∂ = T dS − F_L dL_κ check. The length coefficient partly restates the adopted force definition; these comparisons are not independent canonical proofs.

The checked product comparison gives S/k_B = 2πU_∂L_κ/(ℏc), equivalent under the adopted dictionary to U_∂L_κ = cJ_η. The density comparisons give S/A = P_LL_κ/T = k_B/(4ℓ_P²). Dividing the supplied mechanical coefficient by the supplied temperature cancels the length and produces the numerical factor 2π/(8π) = 1/4. This explains consistency between the normalizations, not a derivation of Hawking thermality or Einstein entropy. The boost-charge interpretation still relies on the cited canonical foundation.

contributions.title: Further source results that remain unverified here
contributions.text:
The manuscript goes beyond the selected checks by rewriting Friedmann acceleration and conservation in screen-pressure variables and interpreting a two-dimensional normal Ricci scalar. Apart from the pressure-to-radius identity already discussed, these dynamical and geometric assertions are NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL. They require Einstein–Friedmann dynamics and the stated metric conventions, not merely the definition of pressure.

The signed Hayward comparison is also unverified context. The source states κ_H^s/κ_CK = (3w−1)/4, a quadratic normal response P_L^H = (P_scr−p_m)²/(16P_scr), and a scale-work identity containing both a volume term and −(3/4)E_A dw. The dw term must remain when w varies. Its signed radial response is distinguished from both the quadratic normal response and Hayward work density; reconstructing material pressure is presented as an on-shell relation, not a new equation of state.

The proposed translation exposes w = 1/3 and w = −1 as inferred premises for the named radiation and de Sitter specializations. They need confirmation. The source’s radiation example reaches zero signed Hayward rate, where a nonzero acceleration-length chart cannot simply be evaluated. The CK thermal products and thermal family differential likewise have no dedicated checks in this report. These are limits of coverage, not findings that the source results are false. Moving-boundary and higher-curvature extensions are explicitly assigned separate derivations.

contributions.title: Limits of the conclusions
contributions.text:
The report establishes exact identities only for the submitted scalar expressions under their declared definitions and domains. The five models were checked separately; physical compatibility between regimes was not established automatically. Repeated product identities and equivalent coefficient comparisons should not be counted as independent physical evidence.

Source fidelity remains a separate task. The supplied extraction interleaves columns and separates equation superscripts and denominators; the original PDF layout needs inspection. The FRW square-root radius and its positive-radicand branch are not represented by the independent-radius checks. Likewise, the conclusion’s statement that κ is regular at zero does not extend L_s = c²/κ through zero.

The source reports a companion implementation and saved results, but those materials and the cited papers were not independently examined here. The earlier review cited by the manuscript provides no evidence for this fresh assessment. NOT CHECKED BY THIS TOOL does not mean NOT PRESENT IN THE MANUSCRIPT. No contradiction was reported for the tested expressions, and uncovered material is not thereby erroneous.

The manuscript states that no observational data are used. Conditional derivations within the adopted gravitational framework do not inherently require a new experiment. Empirical applicability is a different question, and neither observational validation nor historical novelty is established by this report.

canonicalAssessment.summary: Conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the manuscript, the supplied evidence supports the cited scalar-sector antecedents, the polarization algebra, and the surface-gravity-to-length pullback. It does not independently establish the manuscript’s complete selected Einstein–Hilbert boundary response: the companion calculation is described but not supplied, and normalization, clock, orientation, other-sector and corner matching remain essential premises. The manuscript explicitly states both \(\theta=0\) and \(\delta\theta=0\), its selected action and its endpoint shift; these are not omissions. This is a private, unapproved scientific assessment, separate from any scalar-check report, not a full-proof assessment or publication approval.

findings.title: Metadata and comparison table
findings.statement: Assertions c003, c004 and c006 accurately describe the supplied abstract, keywords, section headings and Table 2’s stated purpose. The table’s declaration that conventions are matched is not itself evidence that every matching calculation succeeds.
findings.reason: These are descriptive assertions, distinct from the scientific validity of the canonical construction. No retrieved primary-source citation is attached to this finding; its external justification remains conditional.

findings.title: Selected Einstein–Hilbert derivation is not available for inspection
findings.statement: For c008 and c024, the manuscript states a restricted Gaussian-null calculation using \(I_{\rm rate}=I_{\rm EH}-B_0+B_\mu\). However, the supplied material does not contain that calculation, the fully normalized action, the definition of \(B_0\), or its complete boundary-current reduction. Thus the principal canonical justification cannot be established from this evidence package alone.
findings.reason: The fixed Palatini and cut-metric checks are prerequisites, not an evaluation of this selected action. A described companion derivation is not an inspected derivation; this does not imply it is absent from the companion.
neededEvidence: The normalized Einstein–Hilbert action, curvature and variation conventions, and explicit definitions of the subtracted and added boundary functionals.
The supplied local calculation showing all boundary, exact-variation and corner terms before the restricted response is extracted.

findings.title: Null geometry, normalization and variable inaffinity
findings.statement: The expansion definition in c065 and the distinction between inverse-length inaffinity \(\hat\kappa\) and acceleration-valued \(\kappa=c^2\hat\kappa\) are explicit. Assertion c094 is compatible with a fixed clock prescription: geometry can vary while that prescription remains fixed. It does not establish the existence of every desired source variation.
findings.reason: Under \(\xi\mapsto f\xi\), inaffinity changes as \(\hat\kappa\mapsto f\hat\kappa+\xi(f)\); a specified normal and parameter are indispensable. A null generator has no proper-time normalization. The 2023 discussion distinguishes affine NEH representatives from normalized Killing generators, so its \(k=0\) statement does not require this manuscript’s physical \(\kappa\) to vanish.
neededEvidence: The precise generator/parameter prescription and admissible nearby geometries realizing nonzero \(\delta\kappa\) with the other stated restrictions.

findings.title: 2016 scalar canonical antecedent
findings.statement: For c069, c072, c134 and c285, the supplied arXiv:1611.03096v2 passages support the area/scalar canonical structure. In four dimensions their scalar momentum contains \(-[\hat\kappa+\theta/2]\), consistent with the manuscript’s \(\mu\). Their bulk decomposition also retains generator and shear terms and separate corner/exact-variation contributions.
findings.reason: The cited preprint is the 2016 antecedent published in 2017. This supports the scalar structure under its conventions, not an independently established SI prefactor or the manuscript’s complete selected action.
neededEvidence: An explicit restoration of the source’s overall gravitational normalization and matching of its generator and measure to the manuscript’s.

findings.title: 2023 correspondence requires a normalization and normal map
findings.statement: For c078 and c135, the 2023 conformal polarization explicitly uses \(\delta(\theta+2k)\), whereas the manuscript uses \(\delta\mu\). They agree as scalar sources when \(k=\hat\kappa\), with matched expansion and normal: \(\theta+2k=2\mu\). With a common restored Einstein–Hilbert normalization, \(\epsilon_{\mathcal N}\delta(\theta+2k)/(16\pi G)=\epsilon_{\mathcal N}\delta\mu/(8\pi G)\).
findings.reason: This explains the apparent factor of two without presuming identical suppressed prefactors. The 2023 treatment also changes spin-1/covariance details and boundary conditions; it is not interchangeable with every 2016 polarization. Table 2’s \(k\) is null inaffinity, not FRW spatial curvature.
neededEvidence: The explicit overall-prefactor, normal, measure and corner dictionary for the two cited versions.
Identification of the selected allowed normal variations rather than only equality of scalar expressions.

findings.title: Exact polarization exchange and canonical two-form
findings.statement: Assertions c060, c061, c074, c075, c077 and the polarization part of c100 are supported: at fixed integration domain, \(-\mu\,\delta\epsilon_S+\delta(\mu\epsilon_S)=\epsilon_S\,\delta\mu\), and adding a field-space exact variation leaves \(\delta\Theta\) unchanged because \(\delta^2=0\). The boundary one-form remains distinct from energy.
findings.reason: This is a field-space identity for the specified functional and fixed domain. It does not imply that arbitrary changes involving spacetime corner terms leave the complete boundary symplectic structure unchanged, or that source-dependent action additions cannot shift responses.

findings.title: Both nonexpansion restrictions are explicitly imposed
findings.statement: Assertions c079 and c080 are explicit premises: \(\theta=0\) and \(\delta\theta=0\). Consequently \(\mu=\hat\kappa\) and \(\delta\mu=\delta\hat\kappa\) on the selected tangent space. It would be inaccurate to report the tangent-variation condition as omitted.
findings.reason: Vanishing expansion on one configuration alone would not justify dropping \(\delta\theta\). The manuscript supplies the additional restriction. No retrieved primary-source citation is attached to this finding; its external justification remains conditional.

findings.title: Shear, spin-1 and matter responses remain obligations
findings.statement: Assertion c070 is supported by both canonical decompositions. The manuscript says other responses are controlled and retained, not that they disappear. Neither \(\theta=0\) nor its tangent condition alone removes shear, generator/twist, matter or corner contributions. Isolating the scalar response requires the stated control of those sectors to be implemented.
findings.reason: The 2023 paper’s stated treatment is vacuum, whereas the manuscript retains matter. Its covariance discussion also shows why replacing the spin-1 sector or imposing a noncovariant normal restriction is not harmless.
neededEvidence: Explicit allowed variations and the residual shear, spin-1 and matter terms in the selected local calculation.
A demonstration that the scalar source variation does not generate uncontrolled contributions through dependent boundary data.

findings.title: Fixed cuts and the stated endpoint shift
findings.statement: For c136 and the endpoint prescription, the source explicitly gives \(-(A_f-A_i)/(16\pi G)\) in \(c=1\) units. On a fixed transported interval, \(\theta=\delta\theta=0\) permits \(\delta A_f=\delta A_i\), so this particular shift has zero variation without fixing each endpoint area. Fixed cut locations do not mean fixed cut geometry.
findings.reason: Cancellation of this area-difference variation does not establish cancellation of every corner term. Both references retain additional corner data or conditions.
neededEvidence: The complete endpoint one-form and its matching to complementary boundary pieces under the stated local prescription.

findings.title: Orientation and sign are chosen but not independently traced
findings.statement: The manuscript chooses the corner orientation consistently with its negative length-response leg. That is a stated convention, not an omission. Establishing its sign from the action still requires the directed null-boundary measure, region orientation and endpoint orientation to be followed through the local calculation.
findings.reason: The supplied static prerequisite check adopts outward radial orientation. Its sign cannot automatically determine the sign of every null face or corner in the manuscript.
neededEvidence: An explicit orientation dictionary from the Einstein–Hilbert current to equations (14)–(16) and the stationary corner calculation.

findings.title: Physical-clock coefficient is dimensionally consistent but conditional
findings.statement: For c081 and c089, the coefficient \(Ac^2/(8\pi G)\,\delta\kappa\) is consistent with a response per physical time. For example, a length-valued parameter \(v=c\tau\), a restored action factor \(c^3\), and \(\delta\hat\kappa=\delta\kappa/c^2\) give the manuscript’s coefficient. The supplied lines state the physical-clock result but do not display this complete convention bridge.
findings.reason: The time-integrated expression has action units; after division by a fixed stationary duration its coefficient has energy units. Dimensional consistency and the fixed thermal/static checks do not select the action, measure or clock.
neededEvidence: The actual parameter-to-clock relation and restored gravitational prefactor used by the companion calculation.
A derivation that the isolated spin-0 term, rather than an assumed response, supplies this coefficient.

findings.title: Surface-gravity-to-length pullback
findings.statement: For c082–c084, on the nonzero chart \(\kappa=c^2/L_s\), \(\delta\kappa=-c^2\delta L_s/L_s^2\). Therefore the adopted equation-(14) response pulls back to \(-\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_S[c^4/(8\pi G L_s^2)]\delta L_s=-\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_SP_L\delta L_s\).
findings.reason: The fixed canonical-coordinate check establishes the coefficient and minus sign. Equality of the integrated one-forms additionally retains the same fixed measures and admissible variations. This is a pullback of the starting response, not its gravitational derivation. No retrieved primary-source citation is attached to this finding; its external justification remains conditional.

findings.title: Uniform reduction and Hamilton–Jacobi interpretation
findings.statement: For c087–c089, a common length variation gives \(F_L=\int_S P_L\epsilon_S\); a uniform cut gives \(F_L=AP_L\). With the selected action and controlled other sources, \(\delta I_{\rm os}=-\int d\tau F_L\delta L_s\) yields the stated local functional derivative. A constant-source derivative over a fixed stationary interval instead gives \(-\Delta\tau F_L\).
findings.reason: An ordinary primitive of the adopted response at fixed area reproduces this derivative but does not establish a complete on-shell gravitational action or unrestricted source existence. The manuscript itself acknowledges action/counterterm dependence.
neededEvidence: The selected on-shell variational principle and existence of the required nearby boundary-value solutions.
The explicit restrictions making other source variations independent or controlled.

findings.title: Potential derivatives and the indispensable area term
findings.statement: For c032 and c035, the adopted potential gives \(\Pi_\partial=c^2\kappa/(8\pi G)\), \(F_L=Ac^4/(8\pi G L_s^2)\), and \(P_L=F_L/A\). Its full variation is \(\delta U_\partial=[c^2/(8\pi G)](\kappa\,\delta A+A\,\delta\kappa)=\Pi_\partial\delta A-F_L\delta L_s\). The area term must be retained.
findings.reason: The fixed potential-force and product-variation checks support these identities under independent coordinates and fixed constants. Differentiating a postulated potential does not establish its canonical identification with the selected action. No retrieved primary-source citation is attached to this finding; its external justification remains conditional.

findings.title: Reduced scalar two-form and pair counting
findings.statement: For c040, c098, c100 and c310, the adopted scalar formulas satisfy \(\delta A\wedge\delta\Pi_\partial=\delta L_s\wedge\delta F_L=-[c^4/(8\pi G L_s^2)]\delta A\wedge\delta L_s\). Thus pressure is a density for this reduced pair, not an additional independent partner. Identifying this expression with \(\Omega^{(0)}/\Delta\tau\) still depends on the prior canonical response.
findings.reason: The exterior-form identity follows directly in the two-dimensional reduced coordinate space. It does not establish the normalization of the gravitational two-form or reduce the full null phase space to one pair.
neededEvidence: The complete restricted gravitational symplectic potential and justification of its stationary reduction.

findings.title: Work one-form and nonintegrability
findings.statement: Assertions c052–c055 follow from \(\vartheta_V=A\,dL_s\): \(F_LdL_s=P_L\vartheta_V\) and \(d\vartheta_V=dA\wedge dL_s\neq0\) on the independent source space. For c146, the scale leg \(\alpha=[c^2/(8\pi G)]A\,\delta\kappa\) similarly obeys \(\delta\alpha=[c^2/(8\pi G)]\delta A\wedge\delta\kappa\), unlike exact \(\delta U_\partial\).
findings.reason: These elementary exterior-calculus identities establish the stated reduced-space distinction. A one-dimensional family can admit a primitive without making either leg an independent state energy. Spherical volume instead uses \(dV=A\,dR\). No retrieved primary-source citation is attached to this finding; its external justification remains conditional.

findings.title: Stationary area–boost route is complementary and conditional
findings.statement: For c108, c110, c117 and c266, adopting \(J_\eta=Ac^3/(8\pi G)\), \(\omega_s=\kappa/c=c/L_s\), and the same stationary clock gives \(U_\partial=J_\eta\omega_s\). At fixed \(\Delta\tau\), \(\eta=c\Delta\tau/L_s\) gives \(J_\eta\delta\eta/\Delta\tau=-F_L\delta L_s\). The charge has action units, and its product with the rate has energy units.
findings.reason: The algebra is consistent, but primary excerpts from references [11] and [12] were not supplied. Their canonical charge normalization has not been inspected here. The manuscript correctly limits this route: the corner one-form is not a complete Hamiltonian variation.
neededEvidence: Versioned primary passages establishing the adopted area–boost pair and normalization.
The stationary normal-frame evolution and orientation map for the same physical clock.

findings.title: 2013 thermal split supports only its stated regime
findings.statement: For c133, the 2013 excerpts support the static-horizon split into area and rate terms for their specified metric/connection variables and horizon-preserving variations. Restoring the manuscript’s constants gives the rate coefficient \(Ac^2/(8\pi G)\,\delta\kappa=S\delta T\). The reference also states a local-Rindler extension, not an unrestricted moving-boundary theorem.
findings.reason: The independent static connection-momentum check supports its restricted density coefficient. The variable choice, horizon limit, orientation and thermal dictionary matter; this is not proof of the manuscript’s general selected null-boundary prescription.

findings.title: Boundary potential versus mass first law
findings.statement: For c137, the manuscript correctly distinguishes differentiating \(U_\partial\propto A\kappa\) from deriving a Hamiltonian mass first law. The supplied 2013 material supports complementary thermal variations, but does not supply the manuscript’s complete generator-dependent Hamiltonian calculation. No additional \(S\,dT\) term can be justified merely by differentiating \(TS\).
findings.reason: The conceptual distinction is sound; the specified Hamiltonian, symplectic-potential subtraction and possible field-dependent-generator corrections require separate evidence.
neededEvidence: A source-linked Hamiltonian variation for the selected evolution if a canonical mass-first-law derivation is claimed.

findings.title: Stationary realizations and cosmological term
findings.statement: For c126, a fixed-\(\Lambda\) cosmological term contains no metric derivatives and therefore adds no derivative symplectic-potential term. For c196, the stated Schwarzschild inputs give \(L_\kappa=2R_H\), hence \(F_R=2F_L\) and \(P_R=2P_L\), preserving the work leg by its Jacobian. This preserves canonical status only if the prior selected response holds.
findings.reason: Rindler distance fixes the length convention for the stated observer and rest slice, not every spherical radius. Schwarzschild family substitution retains the area leg: \(dU_\partial=\Pi_\partial dA_H-F_RdR_H\). Neither example establishes all other boundary obligations.
neededEvidence: The matching of each stationary realization to the selected action, clock and boundary/corner prescription.

findings.title: FRW is a separately assigned screen prescription
findings.statement: Assertions c127, c131 and c132 correctly restrict the null-action result: zero expansion of a selected null normal on individual cuts does not make the evolving FRW worldtube null and nonexpanding. For c220, the separate Cai–Kim assignment \(L_{\rm CK}=R_A\) makes length and radius work coincide, giving \(P_R=P_L=\rho/3\) under the stated Einstein–Misner–Sharp input.
findings.reason: These are conditional screen-state identities, not a deduction of their canonical provenance from the nonexpanding-null theorem. An expanding null boundary retains \(\delta\theta\) and other-sector contributions when expressed through \(\delta\kappa\).
neededEvidence: A separate dynamical boundary derivation if the FRW screen identities are assigned a stronger canonical interpretation.
Independent thermal-state evidence for exact equilibrium claims during general FRW evolution.

findings.title: Thermal interpretation supplies additional physical inputs
findings.statement: The thermal and boost-charge interpretation associated with c266 requires the separately adopted Hawking–Unruh/KMS temperature and Einstein entropy with zero additive constant. On \(\kappa>0\), these give \(S\delta T=[Ac^2/(8\pi G)]\delta\kappa\) and \(U_\partial=TS\). They do not derive the boundary action or establish a suitable thermal state on an arbitrary evolving horizon.
findings.reason: The fixed thermal-coefficient check tests normalization under these inputs. With positive temperature proportional to \(|\kappa|\), the signed negative branch cannot simply inherit the displayed positive-branch identities.
neededEvidence: Physical justification of the thermal state and normalization in each claimed application, independently of the mechanical algebra.

findings.title: Unprovided 2018 and Kong citation content
findings.statement: For c286, arXiv:1802.06135v1 is listed and cited, but no excerpt from it is supplied. For c253, the manuscript attributes \(P_{\rm eff}=-dE_A/dV_A\) to Kong, but that reference is likewise unavailable here. Their exact contents and convention matches have not been assessed.
findings.reason: Evidence from the retrieved 2016 paper cannot substitute for inspection of the separately cited 2018 version. The conditional derivative \(-dE_A/dV_A=-P_{\rm scr}\) does not establish the attribution to Kong.
neededEvidence: The relevant versioned 2018 primary passages.
The relevant Kong passage defining the cited effective pressure.

findings.title: Applicability, novelty and review-process limits
findings.statement: The selected excerpts and fixed identities do not decide historical novelty, broad physical applicability or the correctness of the full companion manuscript. AI assistance, citation agreement and an archived review are not independent proofs of the specialized boundary theorem. No author approval or publication consent is recorded for this proposed translation.
findings.reason: The manuscript itself limits its prescription and separates longer-paper applications. Selected excerpts are not full-paper evidence; their silence cannot establish absence of an argument elsewhere.

conventions.name: Normalized Einstein–Hilbert action
conventions.value: The selected calculation names \(I_{\rm EH}\), but its complete prefactor, coordinate-unit convention, curvature sign and boundary-current convention are not displayed in the supplied lines.

conventions.name: Null generator and acceleration scale
conventions.value: A selected generator obeys \(\nabla_\xi\xi=\hat\kappa\xi\); the physical acceleration scale is \(\kappa=c^2\hat\kappa\), with a specified clock normalization.

conventions.name: Null units versus physical time
conventions.value: \(\hat\kappa\) and \(\theta\) have inverse-length units; \(\kappa\) has acceleration units. The null generator has no proper time or material proper acceleration.

conventions.name: Parameter-to-clock conversion
conventions.value: Equation (14) states the physical-time response, but the full relation between \(dv\), \(d\tau\), the restored action prefactor and the selected generator is not displayed.

conventions.name: Four-dimensional scalar source
conventions.value: \(\mu=\hat\kappa+\theta/2\). Table 2’s null inaffinity \(k\) must not be confused with FRW curvature \(k\).

conventions.name: 2016/2023 prefactor and normal dictionary
conventions.value: The scalar structures match conditionally through \(\theta+2k=2\mu\). A complete restored-prefactor, normal, measure and corner dictionary is not supplied in Table 2.

conventions.name: Rate polarization and action
conventions.value: Add \(\delta B_\mu\) to exchange the scalar area and rate polarizations; the companion uses \(I_{\rm rate}=I_{\rm EH}-B_0+B_\mu\). Source-dependent additions can change the response.

conventions.name: Fixed integration domain
conventions.value: The selected response fixes clock prescription, cuts and interval while allowing their geometry to vary.

conventions.name: Endpoint prescription
conventions.value: In \(c=1\) units the stated endpoint shift is \(-(A_f-A_i)/(16\pi G)\). Tangent nonexpansion gives equal endpoint area variations, not separately fixed endpoint areas.

conventions.name: Restricted variation space
conventions.value: Preserve nullness and impose both \(\theta=0\) and \(\delta\theta=0\).

conventions.name: Other canonical sectors
conventions.value: Shear and generator/twist sectors remain present; other responses are controlled and matter retained. Their detailed local restrictions are not displayed here.

conventions.name: Orientation and response sign
conventions.value: The selected orientation yields positive \(A\delta\kappa\) and negative \(F_L\delta L_s\); the corner orientation is chosen consistently with equation (15).

conventions.name: Independent mechanical coordinates
conventions.value: Hold \(c,G\) fixed and differentiate in independent \((A,L_s)\) before family restriction. Define \(F_L=-\partial_{L_s}U_\partial\) and \(P_L=F_L/A\).

conventions.name: Signed length chart
conventions.value: \(L_s=c^2/\kappa\), \(L_\kappa=|L_s|\), on \(\kappa\neq0\). Regularity in the \(\kappa\) chart at zero does not extend the inverse-length chart through zero.

conventions.name: Uniform stationary and boost reductions
conventions.value: Use a common source variation, a uniform finite cut for \(F_L=AP_L\), and fixed stationary duration for division by \(\Delta\tau\). The boost route uses the same clock with \(J_\eta=Ac^3/(8\pi G)\) and \(\omega_s=\kappa/c\).

conventions.name: Thermal branch and entropy
conventions.value: Thermality is additional input: temperature uses \(|\kappa|\), Einstein entropy has zero additive constant, and the displayed mechanical thermal identifications use the positive branch.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: The local derivation is described, not absent, but readers need an inspectable normalization and boundary-term bridge.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: Equations (14)–(17) rely on the restricted Appendix I action calculation, not on differentiating the potential alone. Reproduction requires the normalized Einstein–Hilbert action, explicit B_0 and B_μ, directed boundary measure, allowed variations, and complete endpoint one-form.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: Make the scalar factor-of-two match explicit without identifying the complete boundary prescriptions.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: When the normals and measures are matched and k denotes our inaffinity κ̂, θ+2k=2μ. With a common restored Einstein–Hilbert normalization, ε_N δ(θ+2k)/(16πG)=ε_N δμ/(8πG). This scalar correspondence does not identify the spin-1, corner or full variational prescriptions.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: Show which parameter and action-unit restoration actually produce the physical-clock coefficient.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: The conversion to equation (14) uses the specified generator parameter and physical clock. If v is length-valued with dv=c dτ, restoring the c³ action factor and using δκ̂=δκ/c² gives c² ε_S δκ dτ/(8πG). State explicitly whether this is the parameter convention used here.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: Prevent nonexpansion from being mistaken for elimination of all other boundary terms.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: Both θ=0 and δθ=0 are imposed. These restrictions replace δμ by δκ̂ in the scalar sector; they do not by themselves remove shear, generator/twist, matter or corner responses. The scalar source derivative holds the specified other sources controlled as detailed in Appendix I.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: Distinguish the stated endpoint cancellation from a general corner theorem.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: For fixed transported cuts, tangent nonexpansion gives δA_f=δA_i, so the variation of the stated area-difference endpoint shift vanishes without fixing either area separately. This statement concerns that shift only; remaining normal-frame and complementary-boundary corner terms follow the selected local prescription.

proposedSourceClarifications.explanation: Keep coefficient matching distinct from the gravitational starting response and from a complete energy variation.
proposedSourceClarifications.suggestedText: Conditional on equation (14) being the response of the selected action, its length pullback agrees with the coefficient obtained from U_∂. The full potential variation remains δU_∂=(c²/8πG)(κ δA+A δκ); the scale leg alone is neither this full variation nor an independent state energy.

literatureAssessment.summary: Conditional on the proposed translation being faithful, the manuscript offers a potentially useful mechanical interpretation of an established Einstein boundary response: acceleration length becomes a geometrically normalized work coordinate, with a conjugate force and normal-scale pressure. The supplied earlier passages already establish the underlying area–rate response, polarization freedom, inverse-distance horizon energy and boost-time relation. The defensible advance is therefore narrower than a new canonical structure: a coordinated length–force interpretation and its carefully transformed work terms. The supplied scalar report supports the stated algebra under its premises, but does not establish the gravitational action prescription, empirical validity or historical priority. The Schwarzschild construction has substantial earlier pressure-work overlap; originality of the separately assigned FRW screen construction remains insufficiently established. This is a private, unapproved diagnostic review, not approval or publication of the formulation.

sections.title: Scientific review — Inputs → construction → outputs
sections.text:
Inputs. The manuscript fixes \(c,G\), a physical clock normalization, a finite cut area \(A\), and the selected Einstein boundary potential
\[U_\partial=\frac{A\kappa c^2}{8\pi G}=\frac{c^4A}{8\pi G L_s},\qquad L_s=\frac{c^2}{\kappa}\ne0.\]
Area and signed acceleration length are independent differentiation coordinates before any horizon-family restriction. This is a specified boundary prescription, not an independently derived matter energy or a universal choice of gravitational energy.

Construction. First differentiate the potential, defining the area response and negative length derivative. This gives
\[\Pi_\partial=\frac{c^4}{8\pi G L_s},\quad F_L=\frac{c^4A}{8\pi G L_s^2},\quad P_L=\frac{F_L}{A}=\frac{\kappa^2}{8\pi G},\]
\[dU_\partial=\Pi_\partial dA-F_LdL_s.\]
The proposed canonical justification is a second, physically substantive step. Starting from the established scalar null datum \(\mu=\widehat\kappa+\theta/2\), the manuscript exchanges area and rate polarizations and restricts to \(\theta=\delta\theta=0\). With fixed clock, cuts, interval and controlled other responses, it adopts
\[\Theta_\kappa^{(0)}=\frac{c^2}{8\pi G}\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_S\,\delta\kappa.\]
Changing coordinates gives \(\Theta_L^{(0)}=-\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_SP_L\delta L_s\), and for a uniform cut, \(-\int d\tau F_L\delta L_s\). The action prescription and physical-time conversion are essential inputs to this identification; differentiating \(U_\partial\) alone cannot establish them.

Claimed outputs. The manuscript interprets \(F_L\) as a generalized boundary force and \(P_L\) as its normal-scale response density. Its \(F_L=M_\partial\kappa\), with \(M_\partial=U_\partial/c^2\), is an identity, not a material equation of motion. A complementary stationary route uses \(J_\eta=Ac^3/(8\pi G)\), \(\omega_s=\kappa/c\), and \(\eta=c\Delta\tau/L_s\) to obtain the same coefficient per unit duration.

Family outputs require additional inputs. Infinity-normalized Schwarzschild data give \(L_\kappa=2R_H\), \(U_\partial=Mc^2/2\), and \(F_LdL_\kappa=M\kappa dR_H=P_RdV_H\), with \(P_R=2P_L\). The separately assigned instantaneous Cai–Kim screen instead sets \(L_{CK}=R_A\), uses \(E_A=\rho V_A=c^4R_A/(2G)\), and obtains \(U_\partial=E_A\), \(P_R=P_L=\rho/3\). Thermal identifications require the additional temperature and entropy dictionary.

sections.title: Scientific review — What the construction means
sections.text:
The most faithful intuitive account is that the boundary has an area variable and a rate variable. The paper asks whether changing that rate can be described as mechanical work against a geometrically meaningful length. In Rindler geometry, \(c^2/a\) is the observer–horizon distance on the observer's instantaneous rest slice. This supplies a geometric normalization rather than merely a dimensional length estimate. On a general null boundary, however, the generator's inaffinity is not a material observer's proper acceleration; the clock prescription connecting these quantities must remain explicit.

Changing from rate to inverse rate changes its conjugate coefficient by the chain rule. The proposed force is therefore not an extra interaction or an additional canonical degree of freedom. Its possible physical significance is that, for the selected action and clock, the established scalar boundary response acquires the dimensions and work interpretation of a force acting through an acceleration-length variation. Pressure is that response divided by the cut area, not a third independent canonical partner.

The distinction between surface stress and normal-scale pressure matters. \(\Pi_\partial\) has energy-per-area units, whereas \(P_L\) has ordinary pressure units. Their relation \(d\Pi_\partial=-P_LdL_s\) compares boundary configurations; it does not describe a pressure gradient through a material layer. Likewise, \(A\,dL_s\) is a work one-form, not generally the differential of an enclosed volume: \(d(A\,dL_s)=dA\wedge dL_s\).

This explains the Schwarzschild factor of two. Because \(L_\kappa=2R_H\), work conservation requires \(F_R=2F_L=M\kappa\), not the same coefficient multiplying both displacements. Consequently \(P_R=2P_L\). Along this constrained family the area term is twice the radial work term, leaving \(dU_\partial=P_RdV_H\). The mass-energy law remains \(d(Mc^2)=T\,dS\); adding this boundary work as another independent term would double-count the same family variation.

For the Cai–Kim screen, the assigned length equals the areal radius, so no factor of two appears. The resulting \(P_{scr}=\rho/3\) is neither a claim that cosmic matter has radiation pressure nor a new equation of state for matter. The screen-state law and matter heat-supply relation sort changes differently. The manuscript appropriately does not infer that a time-dependent FRW apparent-horizon worldtube is a nonexpanding null boundary, or that the algebra establishes exact equilibrium thermality during arbitrary cosmic evolution.

sections.title: Scientific review — Established foundations and close precedents
sections.text:
The closest earlier result is more specific than the familiar formula \(TS\). In the selected full-text passages of Parattu–Majhi–Padmanabhan (2013), the horizon-preserving variation separates into an area term and an area-weighted surface-gravity variation. Their displayed relations (111)–(113) give the rate leg \(A\,\delta\kappa/(8\pi G)\) in corresponding geometrized conventions, interpreted thermally as \(S\delta T\). Thus the operational source and coefficient underlying the manuscript's length leg already have a concrete antecedent. Replacing \(\kappa\) by \(c^2/L_s\) produces the manuscript's coefficient once conventions are matched; the interpretation of that coefficient is the issue to assess.

Hopfmüller–Freidel's 2016 preprint, cited in the manuscript as a 2017 journal article, explicitly identifies the scalar momentum involving \(\kappa+(D-3)\theta/(D-2)\), separates boundary and corner contributions, and explains why exact variations change polarization without changing the two-form. Their 2018 passages explicitly discuss the rate-polarized term and switching to an area-fixed polarization by a boundary action. They also explain the clock dependence of the scalar datum. Odak–Rignon-Bret–Speziale (2023) display the alternative scalar polarizations, including \(\delta(\theta+2k)\epsilon_{\mathcal N}\). Restoring the overall Einstein normalization and restricting \(\delta\theta=0\) gives the same scalar rate coefficient, but their corner and covariance requirements cannot be discarded when identifying a particular action problem.

Inverse-distance horizon energy also predates this manuscript. Frodden–Ghosh–Perez's 2011 preprint, cited here through its 2013 journal publication, gives \(E=A/(8\pi\ell)\) and \(\bar\kappa=1/\ell\) for nearby preferred observers in geometrized units. Bianchi–Wieland (2012) derive a horizon corner action and explicitly relate observer proper time to boost angle by \(t=\eta\ell\). These passages substantially anticipate the manuscript's stationary charge-times-rate and fixed-duration inverse-length route; they are not merely remote thermodynamic context.

Membrane pressure is also established, but the relevant distinction is substantive. Kolekar–Kothawala's 2011 preprint, published in 2012, derives tangential membrane stresses and the Einstein-case relation \(p_sA=TS\). This corresponds to the area-response side, not automatically the normal pressure \(P_L=\Pi_\partial/L_s\). Wang's cosmological membrane construction explicitly shows generator and regulator dependence of nonstationary membrane pressure. Faraoni's selected 2011 passages establish the non-null character possible for FRW apparent horizons, the areal-volume convention, and dependence of thermodynamic work allocation on surface-gravity prescription.

sections.title: Scientific review — Precise proposed advance and novelty assessment
sections.text:
The strongest candidate contribution is the identification of acceleration length as a normalized mechanical source coordinate, with the force density inherited from a selected gravitational action response. That is more precise than restating \(U_\partial=TS\), and a conceptual identification within Einstein gravity can constitute an advance without changing its equations. Here, however, neither the scalar canonical pair, its rate polarization, the inverse-acceleration length, nor the stationary boost-time/distance relation can be claimed as newly discovered on the supplied evidence.

What may differ is the combination: an explicit nonthermal length-work interpretation of the rate leg, its normal-scale pressure density, and a common treatment of coordinate changes before and after restricting to horizon families. Relative to Parattu–Majhi–Padmanabhan, the new interpretation replaces the thermal reading of the rate response with a length-conjugate mechanical response. Relative to Hopfmüller–Freidel and Odak and collaborators, it selects a nonexpanding scalar sector and a particular action/clock prescription rather than introducing a new null phase-space pair. Relative to Bianchi–Wieland and Frodden–Ghosh–Perez, the distinction is not inverse-distance energy itself, but promoting length variation to an explicit source-response work term and interpreting its area density. This supports a bounded partly-novel interpretation, not a strong first-priority claim.

The Schwarzschild consequence also needs a close pressure-work comparison. Ong's selected 2023 passages already propose \(dE=T\,dS-P\,dV\), identify thermodynamic energy as half the ADM mass, and connect pressure to a maximum-force premise and horizon fluctuations. Therefore neither half-mass boundary energy nor a Schwarzschild pressure-work balance is, by itself, distinctive here. The manuscript's possible advance is its different provenance: the coefficient follows from the selected boundary response and the Jacobian \(dL_\kappa/dR_H=2\), with no maximum-force or fluctuating-shell premise. The displayed Ong excerpts do not include all pressure/volume formulas needed to decide exact coefficient equivalence under the same volume convention.

The FRW result is a conditional consequence of the independently assigned Cai–Kim rate and the Einstein–Misner–Sharp identification. Faraoni and Wang already show that cosmological pressure and work allocations depend on the chosen rate, generator and boundary construction. The manuscript gives a particular normal-scale assignment, but the supplied evidence does not settle its exact priority: the manuscript's cited Cai–Kim and Kong papers are not supplied as assessed primary records. No new observational prediction is supplied for any of these constructions. The predicted coefficients are conditional consistency consequences, not demonstrated departures from Einstein gravity.

sections.title: Scientific review — Potential contribution to the field's explanation
sections.text:
Established explanatory structure. Earlier work already connects gravitational boundary variations to canonical data, horizon energy, boost evolution and thermal variables. This manuscript does not replace that account. Its plausible contribution is to make the scalar rate response mechanically intelligible as work through a normalized inverse-acceleration length, while keeping separate the boundary potential, action one-form, Hamiltonian mass law and matter-supply law.

Conditional conceptual gain. If the selected action derivation and clock identification are sound, the length–force interpretation supplies a useful account of what displacement accompanies the boundary rate response. The common pressure density and the Schwarzschild/Cai–Kim comparison then explain why apparently similar horizon work formulas have different coefficients: the displacement maps differ. This could improve comparisons among boundary mechanics, membrane stresses and horizon thermodynamics, especially by preventing the identification of an area stress with a normal pressure or the addition of a redundant work term to the mass first law. This is an identifiable conceptual contribution, not merely a claim that familiar equations have been rearranged.

Limits on that gain. Its magnitude is reduced by the particularly close earlier inverse-distance energy and corner-action constructions. Because force coefficients transform with the chosen work coordinate and can shift under source-dependent boundary additions, the manuscript has not established a unique, prescription-independent force observable. Demonstrating a controlled gravitational boundary experiment or a clearly specified source-variation protocol would make the interpretation more physically informative; none is supplied here as a new testable prediction.

Cosmological contribution. The proposed screen pressure can provide a compact representation of the same Friedmann dynamics, but not an independent explanation of cosmic acceleration or a new source of gravity. The manuscript's signed Hayward comparison is useful as a warning against universalizing the Cai–Kim assignment: changing the rate changes the potential and work allocation, and varying \(w\) introduces an additional \(dw\) term. These are conditional interpretations of established dynamics. Moving-boundary, higher-curvature and microscopic extensions remain separate projects, not established advances of this seven-page source.

sections.title: Scientific review — Mathematical, physical and evidence limits
sections.text:
Review and checking status. Author approval and publication consent are not recorded. Conclusions remain conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the manuscript. An actual report is supplied: formal-lab-sympy-v2, SymPy 1.14.0, package digest d57cd0e9c2bcf64a7096d1fbb85ce06062531b149ed7f262054ed161eaf4bf47. All displayed scalar entries have status checked, residual zero and consistent dimensions; no contradicted or inconclusive entry appears in this report. Examples include b1-g01_length_coefficient and b1-g01_pressure_accel_formula; b2-g02_null_pressure_coefficient and b2-g02_corner_force_coefficient; b3-g03_firstlaw_area and b3-g03_firstlaw_length; b4-g04_c184 and b4-g04_c185; and b5-g05_density and b5-g05_family_law. These establish conditional scalar identities, not the entire paper. Several entries restate definitions or share algebraic content.

Canonical gap. The checker adopts the physical response in manuscript equation (14). Its restricted constant-source action derivative, b2-g02_constant_source_action_derivative, differentiates a primitive of that adopted response; it is not an independent derivation from Einstein–Hilbert metric variations. The companion Appendix I, including its metric/variation jets and endpoint treatment, is not supplied. The seven-page source specifies an endpoint shift and argues that tangent nonexpansion cancels its variation, but the complete local calculation cannot be assessed here. Full functional derivatives, field-space forms, other canonical sectors, source realizability and global corner consistency remain outside the scalar report. Nonexpansion alone should not be silently strengthened to shear-free or flux-free conditions without the additional assumptions required; the selected Shi and Adami passages illustrate why these distinctions matter.

Physical scope. The length chart excludes \(\kappa=0\), even though the rate chart can remain regular there. The thermal formulas use the positive branch and independently adopted Hawking–Unruh/KMS and Einstein-entropy normalizations. They do not derive thermality or the entropy coefficient from mechanics alone. The FRW scalar checks do not establish the horizon-radius relation to \(H,a,k\), cosmic-time dynamics, the normal-curvature equation, or the signed Hayward reconstruction. The generic action result does not automatically apply to an evolving FRW worldtube. No observational data or new empirical discrimination is provided.

Sources and literature. The extracted two-column equations have layout ambiguities; the original PDF layout has not been independently inspected in this review. Fourteen assessed papers supply targeted selected passages, not complete-paper readings; the remaining ten supply abstracts. Some closely relevant equations are absent even from the selected excerpts, notably the full Ong pressure/volume comparison. Other cited primary works, including the Cai–Kim and Kong comparisons, are not assessed records here. The search audit has no unresolved latest retrieval failures; missing comparison coverage should not be represented as a currently failed lookup. This finite search cannot certify exhaustive novelty.

Chronology. The sole present-date reference is 2026-10-28T19:52:33.472Z. The manuscript's explicit revision date, 28 October 2026, is not future-dated relative to it. None of the assessed records has a supplied date later than that reference; the April, May, July and August 2026 records are therefore not future literature. Preprint submission years must be distinguished from later journal years, including the 2016/2017 Hopfmüller–Freidel and 2011/2013 Frodden–Ghosh–Perez cases. Exact dates of all displayed revisions and the manuscript's first circulation are not supplied, limiting version-specific priority conclusions. The manuscript's reference to an earlier review is not evidence for this fresh formulation.

Comparison of the earlier fixed-distance variation protocol with the proposed variable-length source protocol.

A side-by-side comparison of displacement, energy definition, sign and numerical coefficient.

overall.judgment: Conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the numbered manuscript, its principal construction is scientifically coherent and supported in its stated restricted domain. tabSummaries.title: What displacement accompanies the boundary rate response?
tabSummaries.text: The paper answers this question by changing from surface gravity to acceleration length. Its force is the coefficient conjugate to that chosen displacement, and pressure is its density over the cut. Changing to areal radius must transform the coefficient: Schwarzschild gives \(F_R=2F_L\), whereas the assigned Cai–Kim screen gives \(F_R=F_L\). This makes otherwise similar horizon-work formulas mechanically distinguishable.

The selected work leg is not the entire energy differential.
The construction requires no enclosed-volume assumption.

tabSummaries.title: Length-conjugate force and normal pressure from horizon boundary mechanics

The resulting Schwarzschild and instantaneous-equilibrium FRW applications are coherent under their separate inputs. Relative to examined earlier work, the contribution is the explicit nonthermal length-work interpretation and its coordinated pressure transformations. Its utility is to distinguish response directions, clock prescriptions and work allocations without adding a new interaction or double-counting the mass first law.

The Hayward extension needs one explicit fixed-variable convention.

sections.title: Acceleration length, generalized force and normal-scale pressure
sections.text:
The central construction starts from the specified Einstein boundary potential, not from a material force law:
\[U_\partial(A,L_s)=\frac{A\kappa c^2}{8\pi G}=\frac{c^4A}{8\pi G L_s},\qquad L_s=\frac{c^2}{\kappa}.\]
With independent area and signed nonzero length, the supported derivatives give
\[\Pi_\partial=\frac{c^4}{8\pi G L_s},\qquad F_L=-\left(\frac{\partial U_\partial}{\partial L_s}\right)_A=\frac{Ac^4}{8\pi G L_s^2},\qquad P_L=\frac{F_L}{A}=\frac{\kappa^2}{8\pi G}.\]
Consequently \(dU_\partial=\Pi_\partial dA-F_LdL_s\). The area coefficient is a surface stress, with energy-per-area units; the normal coefficient is a pressure density. Its force interpretation gains physical content from matching the selected action response, discussed below, rather than from the derivative definition alone.

The products \(U_\partial=\Pi_\partial A=F_LL_s=P_LAL_s\) describe one potential, not separate energy stores. Similarly, \(F_L=M_\partial\kappa\) uses the potential's mass equivalent and is not a new material equation of motion. The pressure is a configuration-space stress slope, not a gradient through a layer of matter. No enclosed volume is required: \(\vartheta_V=A\,dL_s\) is generally not exact because \(d\vartheta_V=dA\wedge dL_s\). A spherical volume instead has \(dV=A\,dR\), requiring the corresponding work coefficient to be transformed.

sections.title: What the Rindler normalization establishes
sections.text:
For the reference observer at \(\rho=0\), the supplied transformation
\[X^0=(\rho+c^2/a)\sinh(a\tau/c),\qquad X^1=(\rho+c^2/a)\cosh(a\tau/c)\]
pulls Minkowski space back to
\[ds^2=-c^2(1+a\rho/c^2)^2d\tau^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2.\]
The calculated acceleration at the reference observer is \(a\), and constant-\(\tau\) slices are orthogonal to its velocity. Their normal proper distance to the wedge boundary is \(c^2/a\). The independent transverse patch has area \(\int dy\,dz\), unrelated to a spherical projection.

These actual checks justify the manuscript's geometric normalization for that observer and simultaneity convention. Dimensional analysis alone would leave a dimensionless coefficient; matching this distance fixes its positive-magnitude value. The result does not turn a null generator into a material observer, establish a force from geometry alone or make \(c^2/|\kappa|\) a universal curved-horizon proper distance. The manuscript explicitly avoids those stronger interpretations.

sections.title: From the local Einstein–Hilbert flux to length work
sections.text:
The canonical foundation is stronger than a potential substitution. The separately supplied companion, 'Restricted Einstein–Hilbert null-boundary derivation — Appendix I of revised full manuscript, matching author-supplied TeX', specifies its fixed Gaussian-null metric, generator, null location, orientation and variation jets. In 'Direct current and the selected boundary action', lines 66–130, it decomposes the oriented EH flux as
\[\Theta_{\rm EH}=C\int\!\left[-\mu\,\delta\epsilon_S+\frac{\epsilon_S}{2}\sigma^{AB}h_{AB}+\delta\{\epsilon_S(\widehat\kappa+\theta)\}\right]du,\quad C=(8\pi G)^{-1}.\]
The checking software directly constructs all 64 connection variations and reproduces this local flux and decomposition for a general cut metric and first jets. This is a computed fixed-chart projection, not merely a citation to the scalar response.

With explicit \(B_0=C\int\epsilon_S(\widehat\kappa+\theta)du\), \(B_\mu=C\int\epsilon_S\mu\,du\) and \(I_{\rm rate}=I_{\rm EH}-B_0+B_\mu\), direct variation gives the scalar rate form \(C\int\epsilon_S\delta\mu\,du\), while retaining the shear response. The endpoint shift is \(-C(A_f-A_i)/2\). The checked evolution and tangent-variation argument shows that \(\theta=\delta\theta=0\) throughout the fixed interval implies equal endpoint-area variations, not separately fixed areas. Thus this particular difference has zero variation. It does not cancel unrelated corner terms.

The explicit dictionary \(du=c\,d\tau\), \(\widehat\kappa=\kappa/c^2\), with restored action factor \(c^3\), yields
\[\Theta_\kappa^{(0)}=\frac{c^2}{8\pi G}\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_S\delta\kappa.\]
The checked pullback \(\delta\kappa=-c^2\delta L_s/L_s^2\) then supplies \(-\int d\tau\int_S\epsilon_SP_L\delta L_s\). For a common uniform source it reduces to \(-\int d\tau F_L\delta L_s\). The reduced generating functional and fixed-duration derivative are also checked under the selected on-shell variational premise.

No remaining sign or normalization mismatch is identified in this chain. Its conditions remain physical: selected polarization, fixed generator and clock, admissible tangent variations and controlled shear, matter, other-boundary and corner responses. Negative controls confirm these restrictions. An exact counterterm can shift the one-form while preserving its two-form and the chosen algebraic energy. The source acknowledges this prescription dependence and does not require an unrestricted covariant or global-corner theorem.

sections.title: Stationary boost response and Schwarzschild horizon-size work
sections.text:
The complementary stationary route uses the same clock and oriented area normalization:
\[J_\eta=\frac{Ac^3}{8\pi G},\qquad\omega_s=\frac{\kappa}{c}=\frac c{L_s},\qquad U_\partial=J_\eta\omega_s.\]
At fixed duration, \(\eta=c\Delta\tau/L_s\) gives \(J_\eta\delta\eta/\Delta\tau=-F_L\delta L_s\). The area–boost antecedent is supported by the retrieved corner-action passages; the coefficient comparison is exactly checked. It is complementary, not a complete Hamiltonian variation or an independent empirical test.

For infinity-normalized Schwarzschild data, the checked family results are
\[L_\kappa=2R_H,\quad U_\partial=\frac{Mc^2}{2},\quad F_L=\frac{c^4}{8G},\quad F_R=2F_L=M\kappa.\]
The factor two is the displacement Jacobian. With spherical areal volume,
\[F_LdL_\kappa=F_RdR_H=P_RdV_H,\qquad P_R=2P_L.\]
The complete boundary differential remains \(dU_\partial=\Pi_\partial dA_H-P_RdV_H\); area and radius co-vary, giving \(dU_\partial=P_RdV_H\). Meanwhile \(E=Mc^2=2U_\partial\), and the mass law concerns the specified Hamiltonian evolution. There is no independent extra work term to append to \(dE=T\,dS\). The force-length and thermal products coincide pointwise without representing separately stored energies.

sections.title: The separate instantaneous Cai–Kim screen sector
sections.text:
The cosmological assignment is not obtained by declaring the evolving FRW worldtube nonexpanding and null. It separately uses
\[E_A=\rho V_A=\frac{c^4R_A}{2G},\quad V_A=\frac{4\pi R_A^3}{3},\quad\kappa_{\rm CK}=\frac{c^2}{R_A},\quad L_{\rm CK}=R_A.\]
The checked independent derivatives followed by family restriction yield
\[F_L=F_R=\frac{c^4}{2G},\qquad P_R=P_L=P_{\rm scr}=\frac{c^4}{8\pi G R_A^2}=\frac\rho3,\qquad U_\partial=E_A.\]
These are supported conditional screen identities. They do not say that bulk matter has radiation pressure.

With the separately stated \(T_{\rm CK}=\hbar c/(2\pi k_BR_A)\) and Einstein entropy, the area coefficient translates to \(T_{\rm CK}dS_A\), giving the screen-state law
\[dE_A=T_{\rm CK}dS_A-P_{\rm scr}dV_A.\]
The supplied mechanical family coefficient is exactly checked; this thermal reading additionally uses the declared dictionary. It is distinct from the dynamical Hayward law using a rate with the factor \(1-\dot R_A/(2HR_A)\), signed orientation and unified work density \(W=(\rho-p_m)/2\). It is also distinct from matter supply across a momentarily fixed horizon. The supplied retrieved records do not include Cai–Kim or Akbar–Cai primary passages, so no new full-text assessment of those papers is claimed.

The pressure representation of Friedmann dynamics is noncircular when its independent inputs are kept visible. Standard Einstein acceleration gives \(2\ddot a/(ac^2)=-\kappa_E(\rho/3+p_m)\), and conservation gives \(\dot\rho+3H(\rho+p_m)=0\). Substituting the checked \(\rho=3P_{\rm scr}\) produces equations (36) and (37). The apparent-horizon definition and checked inverse-radius pressure relation give equation (35). These are rewrites of the same dynamics, exactly as the manuscript says, not new equations of motion or proof of exact thermality throughout arbitrary evolution.

sections.title: Hayward work retains an independent equation-of-state variation
sections.text:
Writing \(\gamma=(3w-1)/4\), the source's signed prescription gives \(\kappa_H^s=\gamma\kappa_{\rm CK}\) and, away from zero rate, \(L_s^H=R_A/\gamma\). Its stated work decomposition is
\[F_L^H dL_s^H=\gamma P_{\rm scr}\,dV_A-E_A\,d\gamma=\frac{p_m-P_{\rm scr}}4dV_A-\frac34E_A\,dw.\]
This explains both why the quadratic normal response is nonnegative and why the radial volume coefficient can be signed. It also makes the remaining ambiguity precise: the next paragraph identifies \(P_R^H=(p_m-P_{\rm scr})/4\) without labeling the fixed variable. As the coefficient of \(dV_A\) in this two-variable decomposition, it is naturally a fixed-\(w\) response. It is not generally the entire slope along a cosmological history with varying \(w\).

The appropriate clarification is therefore small and specific: state the fixed-\(w\) convention, or give the alternative protocol and retain its \(dw\) contribution. No claim of a new bulk equation of state follows from solving the response relation for \(p_m\). Radiation gives zero signed Hayward rate while the finite-radius CK screen remains finite; this uses the regular rate variable, not a finite inverse-rate length at that point. De Sitter gives equal rate magnitudes with opposite signs in this comparison.

sections.title: Thermal consistency is additional to the mechanics
sections.text:
The manuscript correctly introduces temperature and entropy after the mechanical construction. A suitable regular thermal state supplies \(k_BT=\hbar|\kappa|/(2\pi c)\); zero-constant Einstein entropy supplies \(S/k_B=2\pi J_\eta/\hbar\). On the stated positive branch the checked coefficients give
\[\omega_s dJ_\eta=\Pi_\partial dA=T\,dS,\qquad J_\eta d\omega_s=-F_LdL_\kappa=S\,dT.\]
They reproduce the complete independent-coordinate law \(dU_\partial=T\,dS-F_LdL_\kappa\). The density chain
\[\frac SA=\frac{P_LL_\kappa}{T}=\frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}\]
is also checked. The direct response-density calculation obtains the quarter through the supplied coefficient ratio \(2\pi/(8\pi)\). This is a useful normalization consistency explanation; it does not independently derive the thermal state, the Einstein entropy law or thermality for an arbitrary moving horizon.

sections.title: The added interpretation relative to the closest examined work
sections.text:
Parattu–Majhi–Padmanabhan's 2013 relations (111)–(113) already supply the area-weighted surface-gravity variation and complementary area response. Hopfmüller–Freidel supply the scalar canonical datum and polarization freedom; their 2018 discussion explicitly treats the rate-polarized response and boundary-action exchange. After matching null inaffinity and normalization, \(\theta+2k=2\mu\) accounts for the apparent factor two in the scalar expressions, without equating every complete boundary problem.

The stationary route also has close precedent. Frodden–Ghosh–Perez use inverse-distance energy for preferred nearby observers. Bianchi–Wieland connect corner boost evolution to observer time through that distance. Those results substantially anticipate the charge-times-rate structure. The manuscript's infinity-normalized Schwarzschild acceleration length is not the same small proper distance used by the local-observer first law.

The defensible added interpretation is to make normalized length variation an explicit mechanical source, identify its force and normal-scale density, and explain the changed coefficients under horizon-family work transformations. This appears distinctive relative to the examined passages, while remaining a coordinate- and prescription-dependent conceptual contribution. Ong already supplies half-ADM thermodynamic energy and a Schwarzschild pressure-work law; the present distinguishable route does not require his maximum-force and fluctuating-shell premises. Full numerical equivalence under identical volume conventions requires further passages. The Kong attribution likewise lacks its exact primary passage. Neither gap negates the supported conceptual distinction, but both limit historical or detailed equivalence claims.
