\delta U_\partial=\Pi_\partial\delta A-F_L\delta L_\kappa,
 \qquad U_\partial=\frac{Ac^4}{8\pi G L_\kappa},
 \qquad \Pi_\partial=\frac{c^4}{8\pi G L_\kappa}.
 \label{eq:local-complete-differential}
\end{equation}
If the specified on-shell action and admissible stationary source family
exist with the remaining responses controlled, the reduced
Hamilton--Jacobi statement is
$\partial I_{\rm os}/\partial L_\kappa=-\Delta\tau F_L$
at fixed other sources. The local computation does not prove existence
of arbitrary such families. Fixed clock prescription also does not
mean $\delta\kappa=0$.

For the consistently oriented stationary area--boost pair already
discussed in the main text, $J_\eta=Ac^3/(8\pi G)$ and
$\eta=c\Delta\tau/L_\kappa$ give
$J_\eta\delta\eta/\Delta\tau=-F_L\delta L_\kappa$.
This is a complementary coefficient check with the same area
normalization, clock, and fixed duration. Similarly,
$\delta A\wedge\delta\Pi_\partial
=\delta L_\kappa\wedge\delta F_L$ checks the coordinate change of
the scalar symplectic two-form; it does not introduce an additional
independent canonical pair.

\subsection{Reproduction, negative controls, and retained premises}

The supplied implementation and approved inputs are recorded in the
Boundary Mechanics Review export of 28 October 2026, available at
\url{https://modernscience.space/boundary-mechanics/report/}.
The reproduction package accompanying this revision records their hashes
and permits replay from the included inputs without the full export.

The accompanying verification files contain the unmodified supplied
reference implementation and approved scalar inputs, separate rerun
outputs, and \texttt{independent\_null\_boundary\_check.py}. The
reference implementation constructs all 64 connection variations in
Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-connection-variation}; the independent script uses
the covariant-divergence expression after
Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-current}. Both were executed with SymPy~1.14.0
and mpmath~1.3.0. The supplied canonical run reproduces its 19
derivation checks and four expected-nonzero controls. The independent
implementation records 24 zero residual checks and five nonzero controls,
including an extra endpoint control. These are overlapping checks of
the displayed proof, not independent physical results. Separate supplied
replays also reproduce the 50 scalar identities plus one definition
restatement and six Rindler geometry checks; they are not a verification
of every extension in this full manuscript.

The controls expose the precise restrictions used above:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \emph{Expansion tangency.} Even on a background with $\theta=0$,
 the rate form retains $C\epsS\delta\theta/2$ unless
 $\delta\theta=0$. A fixed coordinate interval with unequal endpoint
 area variations likewise retains the endpoint term in
 Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-endpoint-shift}.
 \item \emph{Shear.} At a cut choose
 $q=\mathbb 1$, $\dot q=\operatorname{diag}(2s,-2s)$,
 $h=\operatorname{diag}(h_0,-h_0)$, and
 $\dot h=\operatorname{diag}(2sh_0,2sh_0)$.
 These jets give $\theta=\delta\theta=0$, but leave
 $C\epsS s h_0$ in the EH response beyond
 $C\epsS\delta\hkap$. This is a local kinematic counterexample;
 it makes no claim about existence of an on-shell nonexpanding solution
 with additional energy conditions. Such extra conditions may restrict
 shear, but are not silently part of this current calculation.

\item \emph{Full energy variation.} The difference between
 $\delta U_\partial$ and the selected length one-form is
 $\Pi_\partial\delta A$, which need not vanish.
 \item \emph{Boundary prescription.} Adding a nonzero local functional
 $\alpha A\hkap$ shifts the coefficient of $\delta\hkap$ by
 $\alpha A$, even if the same algebraic function $U_\partial$ is
 retained. Its exact variation leaves the two-form unchanged.
 Thus $U_\partial$ alone does not uniquely determine the action response.
\end{enumerate}

The demonstrated result is therefore the EH scalar response in the fixed
Gaussian-null domain with the specified boundary functionals, orientation,
physical clock, and tangent nonexpansion. Remaining shear, generator,
matter, other-boundary, and corner responses must be controlled in the
chosen variational problem. No arbitrary-generator covariance theorem,
moving-cut or global-corner theorem, or canonical certification of a
generic evolving FRW worldtube follows from these local checks. These
limits leave the derived coefficient and its length-work interpretation
intact in the declared sector.

It computes the local EH null projection directly from metric and variation jets, varies the explicit boundary functionals, and derives length work through the tangent restrictions and physical-clock conversion. Arbitrary covariant/global corner certification is not claimed.

assumptions.statement: Model 1: This proposed translation adopts the specified Einstein boundary prescription; it does not derive that prescription from an action or establish its canonical justification.
Model 1: c and G are fixed positive physical constants. A is a finite positive cut area. Their positive domains are disclosed physical-domain choices, not recorded author approvals.
Model 1: A and L_s are independent differentiation coordinates, with L_s nonzero and of either sign. No horizon-family relation between them is imposed.
Model 1: The source coordinate relation L_s=c²/κ is represented equivalently by the adopted definition κ=c²/L_s on the nonzero chart. The specified physical time normalization is retained.
Model 1: U_b is defined using the source's area–surface-gravity formula, not its length-coordinate formula. The latter is a proposed substitution check.
Model 1: All declared derived dependencies are expanded during differentiation. In particular, κ varies with L_s and is not held independent when differentiating U_b with respect to L_s.
Model 1: Pi_b is the A derivative of U_b at fixed L_s; F_L is the negative L_s derivative at fixed A; P_L is F_L/A. These response conventions are adopted premises.
Model 1: M_b=U_b/c² and kappa_E=8πG/c⁴ are adopted conventions. They do not introduce a material equation of motion.
Model 1: pi denotes the usual fixed positive dimensionless mathematical constant. Response symbols have real domains so that their signs are not assumed as conclusions.

Model 2: Use fixed positive c and G and the positive dimensionless circle constant pi. Positive finite cut area A is a proposed physical domain choice, not an independently established source conclusion.

Model 2: Keep A and signed Ls independent. Restrict Ls to nonzero values and use the inverse acceleration-length chart kappa=c^2/Ls with the source's specified physical clock. No horizon-family relation between A and Ls is imposed.

Model 2: Adopt the Einstein boundary potential in equation (2). Adopt the explicit stress and pressure formulas in equations (4) and (6); define FL independently by the negative Ls derivative of the potential. Adoption of these formulas is not an independent verification of their gravitational justification.

Model 2: For the canonical interpretation, adopt the source's null hypersurface and spacelike cuts, selected generator, nonexpanding sector theta=0, and tangent variations delta theta=0. Preserve nullness and retain matter and other responses while controlling the other boundary data.

Model 2: Adopt the selected rate-action prescription I_rate=I_EH-B_0+B_mu, its orientation, fixed clock, cuts and interval, and its stated endpoint prescription. These physical choices are not derived from the potential.

Model 2: Adopt equation (14) as the physical canonical input: the response density multiplying delta kappa and the area and physical-time measures is c^2/(8*pi*G). The scalar checks do not establish this boundary one-form.
Model 2: Use a common length variation and, where the integrated scalar response is discussed, a uniform finite cut. The stationary duration dt is positive and fixed.
Model 2: For the complementary stationary route, adopt the matched corner orientation, Jeta=A*c^3/(8*pi*G), and omega=kappa/c for the same area normalization and physical clock.
Model 2: Adopt the stationary boost relation eta=c*dt/Ls. Its differentiation holds dt and all other independent scalars fixed.
Model 2: The independent kappa_src is an alternate source-chart coordinate, not an additional physical degree of freedom. Coordinate substitutions explicitly relate it to kappa or Ls.

Model 2: At fixed A and controlled other data, integrate the adopted equation-(14) response over the fixed stationary interval. I_src is only a primitive of this source-restricted first variation: I0+dt*A*Rk*kappa_src, with I0 independent of the acceleration-length source. This does not assume the desired length-force derivative or specify the complete on-shell action.

Model 2: Ios denotes that restricted primitive after the explicit substitution kappa_src=kappa. No physical interpretation of its A derivative is asserted; a length-independent remainder can depend on other fixed data.

Model 2: Ordinary derivatives translate scalar differential coefficients. Integral, functional-derivative, tensor and exterior-form statements retain their separate physical and mathematical requirements.
Model 3: This is a proposed private scalar translation for group g03, not an author-approved formulation or a verification of the manuscript.
Model 3: For c025 and c263, A and Lk are independent positive scalar coordinates. Work only on the source's positive branch, where L_s = L_κ = Lk and κ > 0. No horizon-family relation is imposed.
Model 3: Hold c, G, hbar, kB and pi fixed during differentiation. Use their usual positive physical values; pi is the positive symbolic circle constant. Positive area excludes degenerate cuts.
Model 3: For c012, use κ = c²/L_s as the inverse-coordinate definition of L_s = c²/κ. L_s is an alias of the independent coordinate Lk, not an additional independent variable.
Model 3: For c020, adopt the selected Einstein boundary potential U = c⁴A/(8πG L_s), equivalently Aκc²/(8πG). Its physical prescription and normalization are inputs.

Model 3: For c029, c032 and c036, define the area response by Pi = ∂U/∂A, the length response by F = −∂U/∂Lk, and pressure by P = F/A. On this branch, differentiation in Lk is the stated differentiation in L_s.

Model 3: For c110 and c111, adopt J = Ac³/(8πG) and omega = κ/c for the same normalized stationary clock and the source's canonical orientation. The canonical meaning of J is not established by scalar algebra.

Model 3: For c258, c259 and c261, adopt the separate regular Hawking–Unruh/KMS thermal dictionary: Omega = κ/c on the positive branch and T = hbar·Omega/(2πkB). This does not establish applicability to an arbitrary evolving horizon.
Model 3: For c262, adopt Einstein entropy S = 2πkB J/hbar with zero additive constant. No entropy normalization is inferred from the mechanical potential alone.
Model 3: For c260, adopt the Euclidean regularity relation through tauE = 2πLk/c. This is a physical input, not a derived regularity theorem.
Model 3: For c269, adopt ellP2 = G·hbar/c³. Scalar differential identities below mean equality of coefficients in the independent coordinates A and Lk.
Model 4: All proposed equalities are conditional on this translation faithfully representing the specified Schwarzschild model; none establishes the physical premises independently.
Model 4: The constants c, G, hbar and kB have their conventional physical meanings and are fixed and positive. pi is the fixed positive mathematical constant, kept symbolic.

Model 4: A, L_s and R_H are independent scalar coordinates during differentiation: A>0, L_s is nonzero and signed, and R_H>0. No area–length family constraint is imposed before the partial derivatives of U.
Model 4: Adopt the Einstein boundary potential U=c^4 A/(8 pi G L_s), the conventions Pi_b=partial U/partial A and F_L=-partial U/partial L_s, and the density P_L=F_L/A.
Model 4: For the Schwarzschild family, adopt infinity-normalized stationary Killing time and kappa=c^2/(2 R_H). This gravitational relation is an input, not derived from the potential.
Model 4: Adopt A_H=4 pi R_H^2 and the areal volume V_H=4 pi R_H^3/3. Areal volume and areal radius are not asserted to be proper spatial volume or universal proper distance.

Model 4: The family has positive kappa. Thus its signed acceleration length and magnitude coincide, and the family substitution is L_s=L_k with L_k=c^2/kappa. L_k=2 R_H is not adopted as a definition.

Model 4: Adopt the inferred Schwarzschild compatibility M=c^2 R_H/(2 G). This is an additional disclosed family premise supported by the source's mass and marginal-horizon formulas, not a separately printed mass–radius equation or an independently established result.
Model 4: Adopt E=M c^2. Define U_H by substituting the family area and acceleration length into U; do not assume U_H=M c^2/2.

Model 4: Use the separately stated radial formula F_R=M kappa as an adopted comparison formula, and P_R=F_R/A_H as its density convention. The work-coefficient claims test compatibility with these formulas rather than assuming F_R=2 F_L.

Model 4: Adopt the additional positive-branch Hawking–Unruh temperature T=hbar kappa/(2 pi c kB), the corner normalization J_eta=A_H c^3/(8 pi G), and Einstein entropy S=2 pi kB J_eta/hbar with zero additive constant.

Model 4: Every derivative along R_H holds the physical constants fixed. Ordinary differential statements are translated into scalar coefficient equalities; this does not translate their Hamiltonian, canonical or covariant foundations.
Model 5: Hold c and G fixed and positive. Treat pi as the fixed positive, dimensionless circle constant, without a rational approximation.

Model 5: Differentiate the generic potential in independent A > 0 and nonzero signed L_s before imposing any family relation. The source relation κ = c²/L_s is expanded directly into the potential definition.
Model 5: Adopt the specified Einstein boundary potential U_base = c⁴A/(8πG L_s) as a physical input, not as a result established by these scalar comparisons.

Model 5: Use an independent positive family coordinate R_A. Adopt spherical marginal-horizon area A_A = 4πR_A² and areal volume V_A = 4πR_A³/3; this volume is not asserted to be proper spatial volume.
Model 5: Separately adopt the instantaneous Cai–Kim assignments κ_CK = c²/R_A and L_CK = R_A. They are not inferred from the nonexpanding-null action prescription.
Model 5: Adopt the geometric energy E_A = c⁴R_A/(2G) and the Einstein matter–geometry identification E_A = ρV_A. Encode the latter by defining ρ = E_A/V_A, rather than leaving ρ independent.
Model 5: Adopt M_A = E_A/c² and the notation P_scr = P_L_CK.
Model 5: Define the area response and length force by the independent-coordinate derivatives of U_base, followed by explicit family substitution. Define normal pressure as force divided by cut area.

Model 5: Translate radius work through F_R = F_L dL_CK/dR_A and P_R = F_R/A_A, using the spherical areal-volume convention dV_A = A_A dR_A. These are scalar work-coordinate conventions, not a covariant action derivation.

Model 5: Positive domains for geometric quantities, energy, density and mass follow the adopted positive-radius branch and definitions. Response symbols are declared real without imposing their proposed coefficient formulas as domain constraints.

sources.title: First Law of Thermodynamics and Friedmann Equations of Friedmann-Robertson-Walker Universe
sources.access: Official arXiv full text available. Relevant Einstein-gravity section read; not just abstract.
sources.comparison: Cai–Kim supplies the apparent radius, spherical energy, matter-supply flux, area entropy and inverse-radius temperature used by submitted Eqs. 29–31 and the paragraph following Eq. 34. In four dimensions its Friedmann and continuity equations become submitted Eqs. 35–37 after substituting rho=3 P_scr. Its matter flux is not the submitted full screen-state differential. Its discussion holds the radius fixed for the infinitesimal flux calculation and describes dynamical equilibrium thermality as approximate. It is an earlier foundation for the assigned instantaneous prescription, not evidence for an unrestricted thermal moving-horizon theorem. The inspected section does not identify acceleration length as an independent boundary work coordinate or derive the submitted general length-conjugate force.

sources.title: Effective Pressure of the FRW Universe
sources.access: Official arXiv full text available; introduction and Einstein-gravity section read in both versions. ScienceDirect landing page fetched as 403, so no claim of reading publisher typeset text.
sources.comparison: Kong defines P_eff=-dE/dV along the apparent-horizon family. In four-dimensional Einstein gravity, E=R_A/(2G), P_eff=-1/(8 pi G R_A^2)=-rho/3 (c=1). These exactly match the negative of submitted P_scr and the same spherical energy slope; E=-3 P_eff V matches submitted E=3 P_scr V. This is a precise mathematical predecessor for that FRW slope and integrated relation, not merely a vaguely related pressure. Kong combines dependent heat/work terms into one total slope. The submitted manuscript acknowledges this and distinguishes its prior independent (A,L_s) boundary differentiation and force interpretation. That interpretive/provenance distinction is real but does not make the shared scalar formula new. The inspected sections do not supply its general acceleration-length canonical derivation.

sources.title: Cosmological apparent and trapping horizons
sources.access: Official arXiv full text; relevant background, horizon causal classification and thermodynamic surface-gravity passages read.
locators: Table 1; Sec. V, first expression in Eq. (91), discussion after (94)
sources.comparison: The established Kodama–Hayward rate is -R_A(2H^2+Hdot+k/a^2)/2 in c=1 units. Combined with the Einstein–FRW equations, it gives submitted Eq. 38: kappa_H/kappa_CK=(3w-1)/4. Its vanishing for radiation and negative de Sitter sign follow from that convention. The earlier causal and thermal discussion supports retaining sign, causal character and prescription distinctions. It does not by itself establish the submitted force interpretation or variable-w work allocation.

assumptions: Four-dimensional Einstein–FRW

nonzero h=(3w-1)/4 branch

steps: Let h=kappa_H/kappa_CK=(3w-1)/4, L_s=R_A/h, and F_L^H=c^4 h^2/(2G).
Then F_L^H dL_s = c^4/(2G) (h dR_A - R_A dh).
Use P_scr dV_A=c^4 dR_A/(2G), E_A=c^4 R_A/(2G), dh=3 dw/4.
Therefore F_L^H dL_s=(p_m-P_scr)dV_A/4 - 3 E_A dw/4, the submitted Eq. 39.
The formula requires the nonzero-rate branch; it does not extend the singular length coordinate through h=0.

mean $\delta\kappa=0$.

For the consistently oriented stationary area--boost pair already
discussed in the main text, $J_\eta=Ac^3/(8\pi G)$ and
$\eta=c\Delta\tau/L_\kappa$ give
$J_\eta\delta\eta/\Delta\tau=-F_L\delta L_\kappa$.
This is a complementary coefficient check with the same area
normalization, clock, and fixed duration. Similarly,
$\delta A\wedge\delta\Pi_\partial
=\delta L_\kappa\wedge\delta F_L$ checks the coordinate change of
the scalar symplectic two-form; it does not introduce an additional
independent canonical pair.

\subsection{Reproduction, negative controls, and retained premises}

The supplied implementation and approved inputs are recorded in the
Boundary Mechanics Review export of 28 October 2026, available at
\url{https://modernscience.space/boundary-mechanics/report/}.
The reproduction package accompanying this revision records their hashes
and permits replay from the included inputs without the full export.

The accompanying verification files contain the unmodified supplied
reference implementation and approved scalar inputs, separate rerun
outputs, and \texttt{independent\_null\_boundary\_check.py}. The
reference implementation constructs all 64 connection variations in
Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-connection-variation}; the independent script uses
the covariant-divergence expression after
Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-current}. Both were executed with SymPy~1.14.0
and mpmath~1.3.0. The supplied canonical run reproduces its 19
derivation checks and four expected-nonzero controls. The independent
implementation records 24 zero residual checks and five nonzero controls,
including an extra endpoint control. These are overlapping checks of
the displayed proof, not independent physical results. Separate supplied
replays also reproduce the 50 scalar identities plus one definition
restatement and six Rindler geometry checks; they are not a verification
of every extension in this full manuscript.

The controls expose the precise restrictions used above:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \emph{Expansion tangency.} Even on a background with $\theta=0$,
 the rate form retains $C\epsS\delta\theta/2$ unless
 $\delta\theta=0$. A fixed coordinate interval with unequal endpoint
 area variations likewise retains the endpoint term in
 Eq.~\eqref{eq:local-endpoint-shift}.
 \item \emph{Shear.} At a cut choose
 $q=\mathbb 1$, $\dot q=\operatorname{diag}(2s,-2s)$,
 $h=\operatorname{diag}(h_0,-h_0)$, and
 $\dot h=\operatorname{diag}(2sh_0,2sh_0)$.
 These jets give $\theta=\delta\theta=0$, but leave
 $C\epsS s h_0$ in the EH response beyond
 $C\epsS\delta\hkap$. This is a local kinematic counterexample;
 it makes no claim about existence of an on-shell nonexpanding solution
 with additional energy conditions. Such extra conditions may restrict
 shear, but are not silently part of this current calculation.

\item \emph{Full energy variation.} The difference between
 $\delta U_\partial$ and the selected length one-form is
 $\Pi_\partial\delta A$, which need not vanish.
 \item \emph{Boundary prescription.} Adding a nonzero local functional
 $\alpha A\hkap$ shifts the coefficient of $\delta\hkap$ by
 $\alpha A$, even if the same algebraic function $U_\partial$ is
 retained. Its exact variation leaves the two-form unchanged.
 Thus $U_\partial$ alone does not uniquely determine the action response.
\end{enumerate}

The demonstrated result is therefore the EH scalar response in the fixed
Gaussian-null domain with the specified boundary functionals, orientation,
physical clock, and tangent nonexpansion. Remaining shear, generator,
matter, other-boundary, and corner responses must be controlled in the
chosen variational problem. No arbitrary-generator covariance theorem,
moving-cut or global-corner theorem, or canonical certification of a
generic evolving FRW worldtube follows from these local checks. These
limits leave the derived coefficient and its length-work interpretation
intact in the declared sector.

overall.headline: Acceleration length supports a generalized horizon-boundary force, pressure and work response within the selected prescription
overall.judgment: Conditional on the proposed translation faithfully representing the numbered manuscript, its principal construction is scientifically coherent and supported in its stated restricted domain. The supplied evidence goes beyond differentiating an assumed energy: it includes a direct local Einstein–Hilbert boundary-current computation, the selected polarization exchange, endpoint treatment and physical-clock conversion. These support the length-conjugate response, while the exact scalar checks support the Schwarzschild and separately assigned Cai–Kim screen identities. No remaining sign or normalization inconsistency is identified in that principal chain. One specific convention needs clarification: the Hayward radial pressure following equation (39) is its volume-work coefficient at fixed equation-of-state parameter, not generally the entire response along a history with varying parameter. Historical priority and the precise Kong comparison remain bounded evidence questions. This is a private assessment dated 28 October 2026, not author approval, publication consent or verification of every manuscript assertion.
decisiveReasons: All 60 submitted scalar candidates have supplied passing exact checks, with zero residuals, consistent dimensions and established mathematical domain restrictions.

The restricted symbolic derivation constructs all 64 connection variations and directly computes the local Einstein–Hilbert null-boundary flux in the stated fixed Gaussian-null chart; the gravitational starting projection is not merely assumed downstream.
The fixed Minkowski pullback, acceleration, orthogonality, distance and independent-area checks establish the stated Rindler normalization for its specified observer and slice.

The manuscript explicitly preserves the distinctions between independent-coordinate derivatives and family restrictions, selected action response and full energy differential, and screen pressure and bulk matter pressure.

The closest examined literature already supplies the rate response, scalar polarizations, inverse-distance energy and area–boost foundations. The identifiable contribution is their explicit length-work and normal-pressure interpretation, not a newly discovered canonical pair.
The remaining Hayward issue concerns a missing fixed-variable label at p6-l027–p6-l031, not an evidenced algebraic contradiction or a failure of the main restricted construction.

metaSummary.title: A mechanical coordinate for the scalar horizon-boundary response
metaSummary.text: Using the normalized acceleration length \(L_s=c^2/\kappa\), the manuscript identifies \(F_L=Ac^4/(8\pi G L_s^2)\), its normal-scale density \(P_L=F_L/A\), and the work response \(-F_L\,\delta L_s\). The supplied local action calculation supports this identification under the specified boundary prescription. Schwarzschild radius work acquires a factor-two Jacobian; the separate instantaneous Cai–Kim screen has a unit Jacobian and \(P_{\rm scr}=\rho/3\). The conceptual distinction is defensible relative to examined antecedents, with historical firstness unresolved.
